title: Chief Information Security Officer
description: Who We Are Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group: education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology. Funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital. The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page. Role summary Catalyst Capital is hiring its first Chief Information Security Officer to own security across every brand in the group. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong. The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers. You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure. What you will own Core security leadership (about half) Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on. Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises. Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline. Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data. Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in. Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders. Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products. Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job. Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording. AI-driven security (about half) Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged. Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work. AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them. Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live. AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Review high-risk agents before launch, including our own security agents. Scope This role protects our company, our platforms, our data and our brands. For members' personal wallets and accounts outside our platforms, our role is education: helping members recognize and avoid scams. Requirements What you will bring Must have 10+ years in security, including 3+ years leading a security function as CISO, Head of Security or equivalent at a company of 100+ people. Has led live-incident response, not just tabletop exercises, including briefing executives during the incident. Has built or rebuilt a security program from an early stage: strategy, policy, tooling, training and incident response. AI-native operator. Uses AI agents daily to do the work: writing detections, reviewing code and configs, reading vendor documentation, drafting policy. Can show us the harnesses, workflows or automations you have built, and knows where AI stops and human judgment has to take over. Deep, current knowledge of AI-specific risks: prompt injection, over-scoped agent permissions, credential and data exposure through AI tools, and insecure AI-generated code. Hands-on with cloud security (AWS preferred), identity and access management, SIEM, endpoint protection and email security. Writes code: scripts, tooling and automation, not only vendor UIs. Experience in crypto, fintech or another high-fraud industry, and deep knowledge of phishing, social engineering and impersonation attacks. Can read the fine print: thorough with documentation, contracts and vendor security terms, and documents everything so nothing slips through. Briefs executives in plain language, trains non-technical staff, and writes policy people follow. Has run a brand protection or takedown program. Experience with customer-facing security features such as account-takeover defense. Experience with risk quantification (FAIR or similar) and presenting to a board. Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GCIH or OSCP. title: Chief Information Security Officer
description: Who We Are Catalyst Capital is a profitable, bootstrapped holding company building a diversified financial services group: education, publishing, software, wealth and tax planning tools, investment products and proprietary trading technology. Funded entirely from its own operating cash. We have never taken outside capital. The cash engine is Decentralized Masters, a DeFi education business that went from zero to 150+ people, 4,500+ paying members and roughly $48.6M of FY26 revenue at ~25% earnings before tax in four years. That engine funds everything else on this page. Role summary Catalyst Capital is hiring its first Chief Information Security Officer to own security across every brand in the group. You will set the strategy, build the program, and personally run the response when something goes wrong. The job is two halves. Half is the core of a CISO's role: incident response, identity and access, vendor risk, phishing defense, policy and audit readiness, and the judgment calls only a person can own. The other half is making security AI-driven: mapping our full surface and building agentic systems that test, monitor and audit it with near-total coverage, so security keeps pace as more of the company runs on AI. This is a player-coach role: about half hands-on, leading a small team of engineers. You report to Group leadership, brief the leadership team monthly, and are the person they trust to explain risk in plain language and make the call under pressure. What you will own Core security leadership (about half) Security strategy and program. Own the security strategy, roadmap and budget across Decentralized Masters, Legacy, Inflection Club, Sentinelis and future brands. Report posture, top risks and trends to leadership every month, with a risk register leadership can act on. Incident response. Own IR end to end: detection, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and the postmortem. Lead the room during a live incident and coordinate with legal counsel, forensics firms, insurers and regulators. Keep runbooks current and run tabletop exercises. Cloud and identity security. Own identity and access across the group: SSO, MFA, least-privilege roles, admin redundancy and short-lived credentials. Set the AWS security baseline. Third-party and vendor risk. Assess the security of every vendor and data provider we depend on, including their audits and attestations, and set the bar a vendor must clear before connecting to our systems or data. Platform and customer account security. Set the standards for login protection and account-takeover defense on our platforms, and work with the engineering teams that own each platform to build them in. Phishing and impersonation defense. Own email security, staff training and phishing simulations. Run brand protection: find and take down fake domains and accounts impersonating our brands and leaders. Policy, compliance and trust. Write and enforce policies people actually follow. Prepare the company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001 with Legal & Compliance. Own the public security and trust story, including the trust page on our products. Team leadership. Manage and develop our security engineers, decide what we build in-house versus outsource, and grow the team only where automation cannot do the job. Member scam awareness. Supply the security content behind scam-awareness messaging to members, working with Community, Support and Marketing. Legal approves the wording. AI-driven security (about half) Full attack-surface map. Build and maintain a living inventory of everything we run: internal apps, cloud, code repos, and every SaaS tool and integration (CRM, telephony, community, payments, data providers). Know what connects to what, who has access, and what is logged. Agentic security harness. Design and run AI-driven systems that approach 100% coverage: automated code and dependency review, continuous configuration and access audits, and vendor documentation review. Humans set direction and make the judgment calls; agents do the exhaustive work. AI-driven detection and logging. Own the security stack (SIEM, Rapid7; endpoint protection; email security; identity and device management), make sure every critical system sends usable logs, and use AI to triage alerts and hunt across them. Secure AI and vibe-coding standards. Set the rules for how teams build with AI: what can ship, what data AI tools may touch, and the review path before anything with customer data goes live. AI agent security. As more of the company runs on agents and automations, secure them: scoped credentials and tool permissions, prompt-injection defense, data exposure, and monitoring and guardrails for agents in production. Review high-risk agents before launch, including our own security agents. Scope This role protects our company, our platforms, our data and our brands. For members' personal wallets and accounts outside our platforms, our role is education: helping members recognize and avoid scams. Requirements What you will bring Must have 10+ years in security, including 3+ years leading a security function as CISO, Head of Security or equivalent at a company of 100+ people. Has led live-incident response, not just tabletop exercises, including briefing executives during the incident. Has built or rebuilt a security program from an early stage: strategy, policy, tooling, training and incident response. AI-native operator. Uses AI agents daily to do the work: writing detections, reviewing code and configs, reading vendor documentation, drafting policy. Can show us the harnesses, workflows or automations you have built, and knows where AI stops and human judgment has to take over. Deep, current knowledge of AI-specific risks: prompt injection, over-scoped agent permissions, credential and data exposure through AI tools, and insecure AI-generated code. Hands-on with cloud security (AWS preferred), identity and access management, SIEM, endpoint protection and email security. Writes code: scripts, tooling and automation, not only vendor UIs. Experience in crypto, fintech or another high-fraud industry, and deep knowledge of phishing, social engineering and impersonation attacks. Can read the fine print: thorough with documentation, contracts and vendor security terms, and documents everything so nothing slips through. Briefs executives in plain language, trains non-technical staff, and writes policy people follow. Player-coach: comfortable spending about half your time hands-on while leading a small, fully remote team across many time zones. Nice to have Has prepared a company for SOC 2 or ISO 27001. Has secured or evaluated AI agents and LLM-based tools in production. Has run a third-party risk program covering financial data aggregators or similar providers. Has run a brand protection or takedown program. Experience with customer-facing security features such as account-takeover defense. Experience with risk quantification (FAIR or similar) and presenting to a board. Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GCIH or OSCP. Benefits What We Offer Competitive compensation package Independent Contractor opportunity Fully remote, globally distributed team Team offsites (Dubai, Costa Rica, etc.) Collaborative, forward-thinking culture that values innovation and results Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Staff Machine Learning Engineer, Home Surfaces
description: The Personalization team makes deciding what to play next easier and more enjoyable for every listener. From Blend to Discover Weekly, we're behind some of Spotify 's most-loved features. We built them by understanding the world of music and podcasts better than anyone else. Join us and you'll keep millions of users listening by making great recommendations to each and every one of them. Surfaces Moments is a ML team within the Personalization Mission focused on creating moment-based experiences across Spotify surfaces. The team owns and evolves the experiences that help listeners quickly connect with the content that matters most to them, including the Home Shortcuts experience and the underlying intelligence that powers it. By combining cutting-edge machine learning, recommendation systems, and product thinking, the team delivers highly relevant, personalized experiences to millions of listeners around the world. As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you will help shape the future of personalized discovery and engagement at Spotify. You'll work at the intersection of recommendation systems, large language models, and production-scale machine learning infrastructure to build experiences that delight users and drive meaningful impact. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys taking models from research to production, driving technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces, and solving complex personalization challenges at global scale. What You'll Do Own and improve the machine learning models and systems that power the Home feed, including the Shortcuts experience. Design, build, and ship personalized recommendations that serve millions of Spotify listeners globally. Build content recommendation systems for emerging agentic and AI-powered user experiences. Train, fine-tune, evaluate, and optimize large language models using techniques such as supervised fine-tuning (SFT), distillation, and parameter-efficient training approaches. Partner closely with product managers, engineers, data scientists, and designers to define and execute experimentation strategies. Drive A/B testing, monitoring, model evaluation, and continuous optimization of recommendation quality, reliability, and cost efficiency. Improve ML platform capabilities, data pipelines, and production systems that support personalization at Spotify scale. Drive technical direction in ambiguous problem spaces and contribute to the long-term architecture of personalization systems. Mentor and support other machine learning engineers, helping raise the bar across the team. Who You Are You have 8+ years of experience building and deploying machine learning systems in production environments. You have deep expertise in recommendation systems, ranking models, personalization, or large-scale content discovery platforms. You have strong proficiency in Python and hands-on experience building machine learning systems with PyTorch. You are experienced with large language model training, fine-tuning, evaluation, and optimization techniques including SFT, distillation, and LoRA. You have worked with large-scale inference systems and understand the challenges of latency, reliability, and cost optimization. You care deeply about creating high-quality user experiences through thoughtful application of machine learning. You communicate effectively across technical and non-technical audiences, and you influence technical decisions beyond your immediate team You know how to design, execute, and interpret online experiments and A/B tests to improve user outcomes. You have experience operating distributed machine learning workloads using technologies such as Ray, FSDP, HSDP, or similar frameworks. You are experienced building and maintaining data pipelines and orchestration workflows using technologies such as Flyte, Airflow, BigQuery, and cloud-based storage platforms. Where You'll Be We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! For this role, you can be within the North Americas region as long as we have a work location. This team operates within the Eastern Standard time zone for collaboration. Compensation Additional Information The United States base range for this position is $227,495- $324,993 plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, 13 paid flexible holidays, paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens. At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Staff Software Engineer (Journeys)
description: 1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that. But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens. We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better. About engineering at Headway: Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!). Principles that guide us: Focus on the mission : We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they’re facing. Ship small, learn fast : We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration Everything is a product : Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind. Optimize for trust : We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes. Tools we use: Languages: Python 3, TypeScript Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix, Next.js Datastores: Postgres, Redis Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, and more), Spark and Kafka Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry Version Control: Github, PagerDuty Vulnerability Management : Snyk, Semgrep Cloud Security: Lacework Delivery : Knock (transactional + product notifications), Iterable (lifecycle marketing + campaigns), Twilio, Mailgun About the Journey Team at Headway The Journey team powers how Headway reaches every patient and provider at the right moment, on the right channel - email, SMS and other communication channels. We’re building the next chapter: an agentic communications engine that learns which message, which channel, and which timing works best for each person — and gets smarter with every send. We own the full stack: from the delivery layer (Knock for transactional, Iterable for lifecycle), to the decision engine we’re building today. About this role We’re looking for a Staff Engineer to be the technical anchor of the Journey team. This is a senior IC role — the person who owns the architecture of how Headway communicates at scale. You’ll design and evolve the decision engine, experimentation layer, and channel orchestration that will define how Headway reaches patients and providers for years to come. You’ll set the technical direction for a multi-vendor communications stack, own the unified message ledger, and bring LLM-powered personalization from concept to production. This role is high-leverage and cross-functional. You’ll work closely with marketing, CX, product, and the patient org — and your work will directly impact patient acquisition, retention, and health outcomes. Who you are: We’re looking for experienced engineers who have the ability to deal with ambiguity and learn new technologies and systems. Below are some additional experiences we think help engineers succeed at Headway. A systems thinker who holds the architecture of a complex, multi-vendor platform and guides the team through it An engineer who has shipped high-throughput, event-driven systems in production and knows what reliability requires A communicator who translates technical trade-offs for non-technical stakeholders and drives alignment across marketing, product, and engineering Genuinely excited about the intersection of AI and communications — and thoughtful about what makes AI-in-the-loop systems reliable at scale A leader who earns influence through technical depth and leaves teams more capable than they found them Experience we’re seeking 8+ years of software engineering experience, with meaningful time at Staff-level or equivalent Designed and built high-volume, event-driven communications platforms — email, SMS, push, or equivalent — at millions of events per month Fluency with multi-vendor delivery stacks; strong opinions about build-vs-buy trade-offs at the platform layer Experience building or working closely with experimentation infrastructure — A/B testing, engagement analytics, personalization, or recommendation systems Exposure to LLM-powered systems in production — not just API consumption, but thinking about reliability, latency, and quality at scale Demonstrated ability to shape technical direction across teams without direct authority Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave. We believe a team's strength is in its people, and we cannot achieve this mission without a team that reflects the diversity of this problem – across race, ethnicity, gender, sexuality, age, national origin, religion, family status, disability, military status, and experience. Headway is committed to the full inclusion of all qualified individuals. As part of this commitment, Headway will ensure that persons with disabilities are provided with reasonable accommodations. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please inform the recruiter when they contact you to schedule your interview. Headway participates in E-Verify. To learn more, click here. A notice to Headway applicants: To protect yourself against phishing and recruitment fraud, please note that Headway only accepts applications through our official careers page at https://headway.co/careers . Headway will never refer you to external websites, ask for payment or personal information, or conduct interviews via messaging apps. All official communication will come from a @ findheadway.com email address. If you are contacted by someone claiming to be from Headway via an unofficial channel, please do not share any information and report it as spam.

title: Staff Product Manager
description: Hi, I’m Geo, Ashby ’s VP of Product. I joined Ashby August ‘26; read more about why I joined here. I’m hiring for multiple Product Managers who will report directly to me. More on the specific product areas below. At Ashby, we have a unique approach to building products . As a PM, your primary goal is to eliminate frustration and bring delight to our customers. You’ll work with engineers who deeply understand the customer and business problem and own the solution end-to-end. This means that you spend less time writing detailed specs and more time with customers and doing deep product thinking. Our unique approach is working. We’re growing >100% year over year and have notable customers such as Notion, Linear, OpenAI, Shopify, and Snowflake. Our growth and retention metrics are best in class among our peers. We’re backed by amazing investors like Y Combinator, Elad Gil, Lachy Groom, and many more! Product Areas From day one, we have aimed to build "all-in-one and best-in-class" software for Talent teams. In addition to building a multi-product foundation from day one, we have also focused on enabling customizability and power-user features while keeping Ashby easy to get started with. Doing both is an ambitious undertaking! We want to continue down this ambitious path in future and add multiple new products, which means we: Are not just building a product, we’re building a platform Need to find a balance between re-usable building blocks and feature-specific behaviour Blend enterprise customizability and ease of use We also want to continuously delight users. We hear "I never thought one could fall in love with an ATS" quite often, and we want to keep that true for all future products we build. We are looking for Product Managers who can own the roadmap and strategy for the following areas: Product Platform: Ashby was designed from the beginning as a multi-product platform. We’re looking for a PM to establish this team and own the shared building blocks, foundational capabilities, and APIs that let product teams move quickly. Great fit if you: Bring strong technical product judgment and enjoy working on APIs, shared systems, and foundational capabilities Know how to balance reusable building blocks with polished, customer-facing product experiences Like creating leverage by helping teams ship quickly and consistently while improving what customers directly see and use AI Platform: You’ll own the Ashby Assistant, Ashby MCP, and the AI platform used across many product surfaces. You’ll help drive shared primitives, such as AI memory and context. Great fit if you: Have experience building AI-powered products, especially agents, copilots, or workflow automation Enjoy shaping shared AI primitives like memory, context, orchestration, and evaluation Can translate fast-moving AI capabilities into products that feel useful, reliable, and delightful During the interview process, we’ll determine which role you're best suited for. We’re also advertising this opening as Senior Product Manager . Both titles describe the same position; please apply once using the title that best reflects your experience. Your Role Drive Impact: Deeply understand our customers and ship impactful product improvements and investments to maintain our strong velocity. Quality: Apply your strong product taste and sound judgement to deliver solutions that are both powerful and a joy to use. Use your judgment to identify areas where we need to improve quality before shipping. Prioritization and Strategy: Maintain a roadmap to ensure engineering is never blocked, and set a compelling strategy and vision for the next 6-18 months. Customer Research: Spend time with customers and customer-facing teams. Synthesize customer feedback, research, and competitive intel to drive smart prioritization choices. Execution Excellence: Set the pace for your product area by identifying bottlenecks, scoping effectively, and driving projects toward high-impact releases. Stay close to engineering work to navigate tradeoffs, manage technical risks, and resolve execution challenges. Cross-functional Collaboration: Partner across go-to-market teams to bring the features and products your team builds to the market. Anticipate and plan for the needs to help inform pricing, marketing, and customer support. Ownership and reliability: follow through on commitments, manage time ruthlessly, respond promptly to stakeholders, and communicate proactively when priorities or timelines change. You could be a great fit if You have an unnatural curiosity and excitement about the end-user and the jobs they do You bring an Engineering mindset to product problems and can think through edge cases and understand how to extend our underlying platform to create leverage You can demonstrate taste - you care about the quality of the products you build and use You're an excellent writer and synthesizer; you bring product knowledge and clarity to the entire organization and enable Engineers with product insights You can build a thesis for prioritization and communicate priorities using a sound strategy that combines principled thinking, research, and data You leverage tools and processes to build operational excellence into your product process You have a strong business sense and understand how product and GTM should collaborate, how your features may be monetized, and how product priorities fit into larger business priorities You may not be a great fit if You prefer to specify exactly what Engineering should build rather than give engineers room to own the solution. You dislike written documentation and prefer to manage the team via meetings and quick Slack messages. You’re primarily interested in shipping features and not thinking through how to make them reusable platform capabilities. You don’t enjoy doing deep research yourself and prefer to outsource that UX research, market research, and data teams. You’re uncomfortable moving with urgency, making tradeoffs, and reprioritizing when new information emerges. You’re primarily motivated by achieving a metric more than delivering a great product experience for customers. We Work Differently At Ashby, the role of Product Managers is different from what I’ve seen in most product orgs. At a high level, PMs are responsible for shipping impactful product changes at high velocity, consistently and over an extended period. When we think about impactful product changes, our primary goal is to remove frustration and add delight. At many organizations, PMs are required to write detailed specs that handle every edge case. Designers are required to mock up every pixel. At Ashby, it’s different. We believe individual contributors do their best work when they have a deep understanding of the end user and the business, and ownership of the solution. This is reflected in the engineers Ashby hires: they own projects end-to-end and deeply understand the problems they are solving. PMs are expected to give significant white space in their specs. As a result, PMs can spend less time managing tickets and more time with customers and thinking deeply about the product strategy. At Ashby, PMs need to be the pace-setters for their product areas. This means they bring a healthy level of impatience and time-paranoia to the table. This does not mean cutting corners or demanding that engineers work unreasonable hours. As a PM, you can help engineers by managing the project scope well, identifying when it’s appropriate to bring in help, or being ruthless about prioritization. For PM roles at Ashby, we believe great products are built through deep thinking and a clear understanding of user needs. A major part of your role involves conducting thorough user research to uncover underlying customer problems and translating those insights into well-reasoned product strategies. Finally, Ashby isn’t simply an ATS. Right from the foundations, it was designed to be much more than that. It’s a platform modelled around how organizations (from early-stage startups to massive enterprises) think about recruiting, managing, and retaining top talent. As a PM at Ashby, you should, over time, get familiar with our most common building blocks. You’ll invest not only in product improvements but in platform thinking. Interview Process If this also sounds exciting to you, please apply. We review every application and aim to get back to candidates within 2-3 days. For candidates that advance to the interview process, here is what you can expect: Intro Cal l - 30 mins Product Experience Deep Dive - 1 hour Product Exercise - 1 hour Final Round Interview - 2 hours Mostly focused on cross-functional Interviews to meet more of the team. This is a critical hire for us and a role that will touch a lot of functions - we want to make sure you'll meet folks you'll be working closely with. Benefits 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby —do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US. We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. Generous equipment, software, and office furniture budget. Get what you need to be happy and productive! $100/month education budget with more expensive items (like conferences) covered with manager approval. $250/month tool budget plus access to Claude, Cursor, and Codex with generous token budgets. If you’re in the US, we offer top-tier health insurance for you and your dependents, with 100% of premiums covered by Ashby. In other countries, we provide high-quality supplemental health insurance for you and your dependents, which is also fully covered by us. Ashby’s success hinges on hiring great people and creating an environment where we can be happy, feel challenged, and do our best work. We’re being deliberate about building that environment from the ground up. I hope that excites you enough to apply. To request reasonable accommodations, please contact hiring@ashbyhq.com. Ashby provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetics, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression. We are committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome people from all backgrounds, experiences, perspectives, and abilities. Ashby is committed to a fair and transparent hiring process. We confirm that this advertisement is for an active, existing vacancy within our organization. Please be advised that we may use artificial intelligence-driven tools to assist our recruitment team in screening, assessing, and selecting candidates for this position.

title: Senior Customer Success Manager
description: About the Role As a Senior Customer Success Manager at NetBox Labs , you will own the long-term success and growth of a strategic portfolio of customers. Your primary responsibility is to ensure customers realize sustained value from NetBox Labs’ products and services, resulting in strong net revenue retention (NRR) and customer lifetime value (CLV) . This role goes beyond day-to-day account management. You will operate as a trusted advisor, helping customers align NetBox Labs to their business and technical objectives, while proactively identifying risks and growth opportunities. You will also play a key role in shaping Customer Success strategy, processes, and best practices as the organization continues to scale. What You’ll Do Own NRR and CLV for a portfolio of mid-market and enterprise customers Develop and execute customer success plans aligned to customer goals and outcomes Drive onboarding, adoption, and ongoing value realization across the customer lifecycle Build executive-level relationships and engage regularly with senior customer stakeholders Partner with the renewals teams and sales to drive renewal and expansion conversations. title: Senior Data Scientist, Artist-First AI Music lab
description: The Music Mission team owns Spotify 's end to end proposition for music creators and the experiences they create for fans. The team is dedicated to building tools and services to enable creation, promotion, expression, and monetization at scale. We're looking for a Senior Data Scientist to join the Artist-First AI Music lab. Our team explores and advances generative technologies for music to create new experiences for fans and artists, with a focus on listening experiences that center and celebrate artists and creatives. All of our products will put artists and songwriters first, through these four principles: Partnerships with record labels, distributors, and music publishers: We'll develop new products for artists and fans through upfront agreements, not by asking for forgiveness later. Choice in participation: We recognize there's a wide range of views on use of generative music tools within the artistic community. Therefore, artists and rightsholders will choose if and how to participate to ensure the use of AI tools aligns with the values of the people behind the music. Fair compensation and new revenue: We will build products that create wholly new revenue streams for rightsholders, artists, and songwriters, ensuring they are properly compensated for uses of their work and transparently credited for their contributions. Artist-fan connection: AI tools we develop will not replace human artistry. They will give artists new ways to be creative and connect with fans. We will use our role as the place where more than 700 million people already come to listen to music every month to ensure that generative AI deepens artist-fan connections. For more information, see this press release: https://newsroom.spotify.com/2025-10-16/artist-first-ai-music-spotify-collaboration/ What You'll Do Lead foundational measurement and insights work for generative music experiences, developing the frameworks that help Spotify understand how creators, listeners, and rights holders engage with generative AI music. Design and run large-scale analyses and evaluations of generative music systems, from prompt interpretation to model output quality, using Spotify's unique behavioral datasets, annotations, and experimentation platforms. Partner with Engineers and AI Researchers to integrate evaluation signals into model development loops, debugging workflows, and product iteration, making sure scientific rigor informs technical direction. Identify the behavioral and market dynamics that shape sustainable consumer demand and creator participation, and translate them into clear strategic recommendations. Build practical, scalable metrics and decision systems that define what "good" looks like for AI music: credibility, user delight, safety, creator alignment, and ecosystem trust. Bring together model, user behavior, and ecosystem signals into clear narratives that shape product strategy, cross-functional alignment, and long-term priorities across Spotify. Create the datasets, dashboards, and long-term measurement systems that give Spotify a lasting, comprehensive understanding of product health and impact. Work closely with Product, Design, Research, Legal, Trust & Safety, Marketing, Policy, and Licensing teams, bringing statistical rigor and principled measurement to help build artist-first systems that scale responsibly. Who You Are You have a track record of using insights to shape strategy for major company initiatives involving many different partners. You have significant hands-on experience in advanced analytics or data science, ideally in a domain involving LLM evaluation, user-generated content, or complex user behavior. You communicate clearly, form well-founded, evidence-backed points of view, and can bring together messy, multimodal signals (quantitative, qualitative, and model telemetry) into clear narratives for senior executives, researchers, engineers, and the music industry. You're proficient in advanced analytics with Python and SQL, have analyzed large datasets, and use AI tools (e.g. Cursor, Copilot) to increase your productivity and impact. You have experience developing metrics frameworks for complex products that help teams measure impact and reason clearly about priorities. You have experience with machine learning frameworks, designing and assessing multimodal or embedding-based models, and validating them against LLM judges or human ground truth, with an understanding of how to evaluate models beyond offline accuracy. You have a solid grounding in experimental design and causal inference, such as A/B tests, quasi-experiments, and power analysis. You thrive when tackling loosely defined problems in ambiguous, zero-to-one spaces. Where You'll Be We offer you the flexibility to work where you work best! There will be some in person meetings, but still allows for flexibility to work from home This team operates within the US Eastern timezone for collaboration Compensation Additional Information The United States base range for this position is $144,714–$206,735 USD, plus equity. The benefits available for this position include health insurance, six-month paid parental leave, 401(k) retirement plan, monthly meal allowance, 23 paid days off, paid flexible holidays, and paid sick leave. These ranges may be modified in the future. Spotify is an equal opportunity employer. You are welcome at Spotify for who you are, no matter where you come from, what you look like, or what’s playing in your headphones. Our platform is for everyone, and so is our workplace. The more voices we have represented and amplified in our business, the more we will all thrive, contribute, and be forward-thinking! So bring us your personal experience, your perspectives, and your background. It’s in our differences that we will find the power to keep revolutionizing the way the world listens. At Spotify, we are passionate about inclusivity and making sure our entire recruitment process is accessible to everyone. We have ways to request reasonable accommodations during the interview process and help assist in what you need. If you need accommodations at any stage of the application or interview process, please let us know - we’re here to support you in any way we can.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Experimentation
description: 1 in 4 people in the US have a treatable mental health condition, but most providers don't accept insurance, making therapy too expensive for most people. Headway’s mission is to fix this by building a new mental healthcare system everyone can access. We started by solving the biggest barrier to care: insurance. The admin work - credentialing, claims, payment reconciliation - is a nightmare. We've automated that. But we're going further. Over 90,000 providers across all 50 states run their practice on our software, serving over 2.6 million patients. We are building the best tools for therapists to run their entire practice, reimagining the experience of finding a therapist, and investing in the platform foundations to enable this at scale, and building much of it with AI. We aren't just a billing layer; we are becoming the platform where care actually happens. We're a Series D company with $325M+ in funding (a16z, Accel, Spark Capital, etc.), looking for exceptional people to help us achieve this mission. We want your time here to be the most meaningful experience of your career. Join us, and help change mental healthcare for the better. About engineering at Headway Building a new mental healthcare system at Headway is only possible because of the scale and leverage that software can provide. The engineering team at Headway is a small but mighty team using technology to build that future (and have a fun time while doing it!). Principles that guide us: Focus on the mission: We view software as a means of effecting change in the world, not as an end unto itself. We write software to empower our patients and therapists to better solve the problems they're facing. Ship small, learn fast: We are building new and novel products and believe that we learn what our users need by quickly shipping and iteration Everything is a product: Whether it's our patient search experience or a developer productivity improvement, we treat everything we build at Headway as a product with end-users in mind. Optimize for trust: We believe that engineers should be continually learning. To learn effectively and to be productive, engineers must feel safe asking questions and discussing mistakes. Tools we use: Languages: Python 3, TypeScript Libraries & Frameworks: FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, React, Remix Experimentation & Analytics: LaunchDarkly, Statsig, dbt, Snowflake Datastores: Postgres, Redis Infrastructure: AWS (Fargate, ECS, S3, and more), Cloudflare, Spark and Kafka Monitoring: Datadog, PagerDuty, Sentry Version Control: Github About the role We are looking for a Staff Software Engineer to own how Headway runs experiments. "Ship small, learn fast" is the second principle on the list above, and experimentation is how we actually do it: eleven teams have run hundreds of experiments deciding how patients find a therapist, how quickly new providers get up and running, whether our AI products are working, and how we collect the clinical outcomes data that proves care is effective. You will own the platform all of that runs on. This is a hands-on technical leadership role with unusually wide reach. You will design and build the core primitives, including how users are assigned to experiments, how we record what someone actually saw, and how we recognize the same person across devices and between browsing anonymously and signing in. You will decide what our long-term experimentation and feature flagging stack should be; we run LaunchDarkly and Statsig today, and that architecture is yours to evaluate and consolidate. You will also make AI a real part of the workflow, from validating an experiment's setup before it starts to catching a broken experiment automatically instead of discovering it in a Slack thread a week later. You will also evolve our experimentation capabilities to expand into market-based testing. Headway is a multi-sided marketplace, so we frequently need to change something for therapists and measure what happens to patients, which changes both how a test must be designed and how it can be analyzed. We need to test whole geographic markets, not just individual users. We need to hold groups out for long stretches to understand real long-term impact. These capabilities are well understood in the industry and we have not built them yet, and they are the ones our business needs next. The job is a platform and a program in equal measure. Half of it is the technical foundation. The other half is raising how well the whole company experiments: the defaults, the review, the documentation, and the education that let a team run a trustworthy experiment without needing you in the room. You will gather needs from teams who all want something different, sequence them into a roadmap, and say no clearly, which means acting as part technical product manager for your own platform. You will sit in the Patient org, where the highest volume of experiments happens, and serve the whole company. Trustworthy results are shared ownership. You will own assignment, exposure, and the experiment data pipelines, which are the parts of the chain that are engineering problems. You will work closely with Data Science, who own statistical methodology, and with the teams who own our event tracking and metric definitions, because a number is only as trustworthy as the weakest link in that chain. Who you are We are looking for a Staff level engineer who wants their impact measured by what other teams can now do. You think in systems, you are uncomfortable with numbers you cannot explain, and you raise the bar for the people around you. You have owned an experimentation or feature flagging stack end to end rather than only used one. Whether you built it from first principles or built the missing pieces on top of a vendor matters far less to us than having been accountable for whether the results were correct. You have built the parts that do not come out of the box: assignment that persists correctly, exposure that reflects what a user actually saw, identity resolved across sessions and devices, or the diagnostics that catch a broken experiment early. You are fluent enough in the statistics to be a real partner to data scientists. You can tell the difference between a result that is weak and a result that is invalid, and you can hold your position on a measurement question with someone who does this full time. You have debugged the hard class of measurement bugs: traffic that split unevenly, users who ended up in both arms, effects that vanished once you looked at who was actually exposed, identity that broke between anonymous and logged-in sessions. You have built a program and not only a platform. You have measurably raised how well an organization experiments through defaults, templates, review, and teaching, not only through code. You have made a build versus buy call on a platform and lived with it. You can reason about vendor risk and about where a warehouse-native approach beats a hosted one. You have landed a migration on teams that did not ask for one, by making the new path easier than the old path rather than by mandate. You use AI as genuine leverage in your work and you have clear opinions about where it must not be trusted without a human. You have driven technical direction beyond your own team through design documents, reviews, and planning cycles, and you regularly mentor senior engineers. You are willing to flex across the stack. This role touches backend services, front end rendering, CDN behavior, and the data warehouse. Experience with multi-sided marketplaces, growth or search and ranking systems, or healthcare is a plus, though none is required. Compensation The expected base pay range for this position is $265,000-$331,000 , based on a variety of factors including qualifications, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, this role may be eligible for an equity grant, depending on the position and level. Comprehensive benefits: Medical, dental, vision, HSA/FSA, 401(k) including match for 2027!, Carrot Fertility reimbursement, and paid parental, medical and caregiver leave. If reasonable accommodation is needed to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and/or receive other benefits and privileges of employment, please inform the recruiter when they contact you to schedule your interview. Headway participates in E-Verify. To learn more, click here. Headway will never refer you to external websites, ask for payment or personal information, or conduct interviews via messaging apps. title: Support Operations Engineer - NAMER
description: Hello! I'm Allie, Head of Support at Ashby . 👋 One of our biggest priorities is improving the systems and workflows our Support team relies on to do their best work as we grow. That’s why we’re searching for a Support Systems Engineer to become the long-term owner of our Support systems. If you love wrangling operational complexity, building durable systems, and being the person a team relies on to keep everything running well, this is the role for you. About this Role We’re looking for someone who wants to plant a flag in Support Operations, with the experience to independently lead a system implementation and the ambition to keep raising the bar as our Support team grows and the systems and workflows we rely on become more complex. The implementation will build on our existing systems and workflows, alongside our Support Operations Specialist, who helps teams use our tools effectively and keeps operational data reliable. From planning through rollout, you’ll work with IT, RevOps, and Engineering to connect the system to the tools and processes around it. Getting the configuration right is only part of the work. Helping the Support team adopt new workflows matters just as much. The configuration, automations, and integrations behind our Support systems will remain yours to own and improve as our needs evolve. You’ll be the person we rely on when something breaks, doesn’t scale, or needs to be rethought entirely. Role Responsibilities Lead System Implementations Own implementation of new systems, tools, and workflows from planning and pilot through full rollout, including configuration, data migration, and integrations with our existing tools. Design routing logic, SLAs, escalation paths, and reporting that can handle more complexity as we grow. Develop and lead a change management plan that helps the team adopt new systems and workflows, with clear communication, thoughtful training, and structured feedback from frontline teams and Support leaders. Administer and Optimize Support Systems Serve as the long-term administrator for our Support systems, owning configuration, automations, workflow improvements, and governance, with access management handled in partnership with internal IT. Keep finding ways to reduce friction for the team and our customers. Document system architecture, admin processes, and escalation paths, and keep that documentation current. Evaluate new tools and integrations as our needs evolve, using structured demos and input from the teams affected. Pressure-test vendor promises against our requirements, recommend solutions, and hold vendors to their commitments after the contract is signed. Partner Across Support Partner with Workforce Management, QA, and Support Training to make sure our systems support capacity planning, reporting, and the technical workflows each team relies on. Be the go-to person for Support tooling, advising on configuration decisions and working with Support Leadership to prioritize the systems improvements that matter most to the team. Role Requirements Hands-on experience implementing or administering a support ticketing system such as Zendesk, Salesforce Service Cloud, Intercom, Plain, Pylon, or a comparable platform. You’ve configured the system yourself, not just managed the project. Experience owning a support-system migration or implementation, from scoping through go-live and beyond. You can make judgment calls when requirements are unclear and see projects through without losing momentum. Vendor evaluation experience with real skepticism. You know how to build an assessment framework, pressure-test a demo, and hold vendors to commitments after the contract is signed. You understand Support workflows, including routing, SLA and priority configuration, queue management, escalation paths, and the reporting Support leaders rely on. You understand integrations, APIs, and data migration well enough to work through technical requirements with engineers. You don’t need to write the code, but you need to understand what you’re asking for and why it matters. You can spot workflow friction, anticipate what will break as we grow, and make thoughtful tradeoffs about what to fix now versus later. Experience guiding teams through system or workflow changes, with clear communication, thoughtful training, and structured feedback from frontline teams and senior stakeholders. You know that a successful rollout depends on how people use the system, not just whether it works. You can build strong working relationships with Workforce Management, QA, Engineering, and Support Leadership. You’re comfortable explaining technical decisions to frontline team members and making the business case to senior stakeholders. You Should Apply If: You’ve worked directly inside a support ticketing system and personally owned a system migration or implementation. You know where these projects go sideways and how to keep them on track. You want to own what you build, including ongoing administration, documentation, and improvement. Getting a system running reliably is satisfying, but so is finding ways to make it better as the team grows and our customers’ needs evolve. You’ve questioned vendor promises and know how to get past a polished demo to understand what a product can actually deliver. You move comfortably between the bigger picture and the details. You can present a vendor recommendation to leadership in the morning and dig into workflow configuration in the afternoon. You like being the person a team turns to when something breaks or doesn’t feel right. When you spot unnecessary friction, you take ownership of fixing it rather than waiting to be asked. You Should Not Apply If: You haven’t worked directly inside a support ticketing system at an admin or implementation level, or you want to manage this work from a distance. We need someone in the details, not above them. You’re looking for an implementation project with a clear end date or lose interest once a system is running. Ongoing administration and improvement are just as important here as the launch. You need a fully defined playbook, stable requirements, or someone else to make the decisions. This role means building the process as you go, working through unclear vendor commitments, shifting needs, and imperfect information. You prefer to make systems decisions in isolation. This role requires close collaboration with Support Leadership, frontline team members, and cross-functional partners to understand what they need and work through tradeoffs together. About Ashby Ashby builds a suite of products that helps talent leaders, recruiters, and hiring managers run their hiring process significantly better. We raised a $50M Series D in July 2025 and support nearly 5,000 customers, including Shopify, Snowflake, OpenAI, Deliveroo, and Confluent. We’re growing much faster than 100% year over year, with a team of roughly 300 people across 22+ countries. Learn more at ashbyhq.com . About Go To Market We view our Support team as an extension of the product itself, one that ensures an optimal customer experience for customers ranging across all market segments. Here are a few points that should give you an idea of what it is like to work with us: We spend a lot of time building best-in-class products since we believe a highly differentiated product is easier to sell. We also spend a lot of time building a best-in-class customer experience. We aim to offer deep expertise whenever we interact with prospects and customers. We strongly believe that small teams with very talented people and the right work environment deliver much better performance than teams with large headcount. We value a strong sense of ownership, principled thinking over experience, and thoughtful communication (we put a lot of effort into using the right communication channels) - we’ll get into these and other values during the hiring process. You can take a look at our Leadership Principles to get a sense of what we value in People Leaders at Ashby. Interview process Our interview process is thorough and designed to give you enough information to assess whether Ashby is the right fit for you, while helping us evaluate technical leadership, people management, communication, judgment, and cross-functional collaboration. Intro call with Recruiting — 30 min Hiring Manager interview — 45 min Take-home assessment - 5 days to complete Sr. Leadership interview — 45 min Virtual Onsite — 75 min Support Partnerships — 30 min Cross-Functional Systems Management — 30 min Closing Questions — 15 min Founder interview — 30 min Benefits Benefits vary by country and are shared in more detail during the process. International employees receive statutory benefits and, where available, employer-paid supplemental health coverage. 10-year exercise window for stock options. You shouldn’t feel pressure to purchase stock options if you leave Ashby—do it when you feel financially comfortable. Unlimited PTO with four weeks recommended per year. Expect “Vacation?” in our one-on-one agenda until you start taking it 😅 Twelve weeks of fully paid family leave in the US . We plan to expand this to employees in other countries as situations arise. A $1,200 annual learning and professional-development budget. A one-time $2,000 home-office setup budget for furniture, monitors, peripherals, and ergonomic equipment, plus a company-provided laptop. Extended health benefits for you and your dependents (subject to availability with our Employer of Record) Opportunities to spend time with teammates through an annual company offsite, team offsites, local meetups, and virtual events. description: About Welocalize Welocalize, a Welo Global brand, serves localization teams through AI-enabled multilingual content solutions that enable enterprises to operate and scale globally. Welocalize combines AI, automation, and human expertise to support enterprises in more than 300 languages, enabling accurate, culturally aligned, and compliant multilingual content at scale. Welocalize’s Opal Platform comprises patented technology designed to automate multilingual content and improve workflow performance for enterprises. Opal functions as an agentic system that orchestrates AI, automation, and human expertise to coordinate content workflows across the lifecycle, improving speed, scalability, and operational control for global enterprises. These solutions operate within a secure and compliant environment supported by seven ISO certifications. Welocalize is headquartered in New York with offices worldwide. welocalize.com Overview The German Translator role focuses on delivering high-quality translations across various content types using standard CAT tools and adhering strictly to client-specific guidelines and processes. It involves continuous quality improvement through feedback, training, and collaboration, while meeting key performance indicators in productivity, quality, and timeliness. Job Responsibilities The following is a non-exhaustive list of responsibilities and areas of ownership for this role: Perform translations in various translation tools for assigned clients and projects Translate various types of content, e.g. marketing, help, UI, or regulated content Support the team with copy-edit tasks on selected content types Master the standard CAT tools and tools associated with translation work for internal clients (e.g. tools for creating queries or checking the live UI elements) Precisely follow the established translation process, e.g. always raise queries when there is a need to Precisely follow the style guide and overall client requirements Improve based on the corrections made by senior team members as well as the client reviewers Keep track of personal error statistics and work on the weak spots Take part in the internal trainings and the ones organized by the clients Participate in the error arbitration process Meet the KPIs in terms of productivity, on time delivery and quality Take part in the internal quality meetings and the quality calls organized by the client for the whole team Constantly analyze own gaps and think of what assistance the senior members can provide to help address those Meet the goals set by the team manager Experience and Skills Native-level fluency in German language Fluency in English, both written and spoken 2-4 years of experience in translation/localization/editing or content writing Good understanding of the localization process Good user experience of standard software, such as Windows and Office applications Good user experience of standard CAT tools, e.g. XTM, SDL Studio and issue tracking and query management tools, e.g. JIRA Ability to learn new localization tools and applications quickly Excellent interpersonal, written and verbal communication skills Ability to work with tight deadlines Ability to effectively present information and respond to questions from groups of managers, clients, customers, linguists Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in Ability to work within a virtual team Fast learner, motivated, versatile Education Level University degree in Translation/Applied Languages/Linguistic Studies or equivalent combination of education and experience (University degree in other fields plus 2 years of full time experience in translation; OR 5 years of full time professional experience in translating) Compensation Additional Information Job Reference: #LI-JC1

title: German Advertising Reviewer
description: Location: Spain, Remote (Work from Home) Type: Freelance, Part-time, Flexible Hours About the Role: We are looking for a passionate and tech-savvy individual to join our team as a German Advertising Reviewer. In this role, you will be responsible for reviewing and grading internet advertisements to ensure they are relevant, accurate, and delivered effectively to end users. This is a fantastic opportunity for someone who loves surfing the internet, uses major search engines frequently, and enjoys understanding what people want based on a few keywords. If you enjoy researching topics online and want a flexible and fun side job, this position is perfect for you! Key Responsibilities: - Evaluate the quality and relevance of online advertisements in German. - Assess ad content and placement to ensure they meet specific criteria and guidelines. - Provide feedback and suggestions to improve ad quality and effectiveness. - Conduct keyword research to understand user intent and enhance ad targeting. - Collaborate with the team to identify trends and improve ad delivery strategies. Qualifications: - Native-level in German and strong understanding of German culture and online trends. - Proficiency in English for communication and reporting purposes. - Regular user of major search engines and social media platforms. - Excellent research skills and ability to analyze information quickly. - Detail-oriented with strong analytical and problem-solving skills. - Reliable internet connection and a suitable home working environment. Ideal Candidate: - Surfs the internet daily and is familiar with various online platforms. - Has experience using major search engines like Google, Bing, etc. - Understands what people want based on minimal information or keywords. - Enjoys researching and learning about new topics online. - Seeks a flexible, remote job that can be balanced with other commitments. Benefits: - Flexible working hours that fit your schedule. - Work from the comfort of your home (based in Spain). - Gain insights into the digital advertising industry. - Enhance your research and analytical skills. - Be part of a dynamic and supportive team. How to Apply: If you are interested in this exciting opportunity, please submit your resume by clicking apply below, we look forward to hearing from you! Compensation Additional Information About Welocalize Welocalize is an award-winning global data and translation company with offices across the world. We’ve quietly worked on some of the biggest tech projects in history, from data localization and translation to generative AI and deep learning. When you join Welocalize, you’ll have the opportunity to bring your career to the next level: - Structured learning opportunities that grow your skills, knowledge, and specialties - 24-hour, 6-day-a--week real human support from our Community Experience Team - Access to long-term partnerships and unique projects across a variety of industries and content types - Corporate and executive career opportunities to bolster your resume and grow your career

title: Account Executive – Steuerkanzleien (m/w/d) | Remote, Deutschland
description: Als Account Executive (m/w/d) – Steuerkanzleien gewinnst du die Steuerkanzleien in deiner Region für Pennylane – vom ersten Gespräch über die Demo bis zur Unterschrift, häufig persönlich vor Ort in der Kanzlei. Du bist Owner des Umsatzes in deiner Region und machst Pennylane dort zur bevorzugten Plattform für Kanzleien und ihre Mandanten. In Frankreich ist Pennylane in diesem Segment innerhalb von fünf Jahren zum Marktführer geworden. Du übernimmst das in Frankreich bewährte Playbook, entwickelst es gemeinsam mit dem Team für den deutschen Kanzleimarkt weiter und bringst zurück, was in deiner Region funktioniert. Du berichtest an den Team Lead Sales – Steuerkanzleien in Berlin. Unser Prozess: Erstgespräch, Interview mit dem Hiring-Team, Case Study, Gespräch mit deinen künftigen AE-Kolleg:innen, Abschlussgespräch mit dem Head of Sales – alles remote, Feedback nach jeder Runde innerhalb von 48 Stunden. Standort Remote Deutschland: Du arbeitest aus dem Homeoffice in einer Region mit vielen Steuerkanzleien. Zwei Account Executives verkaufen bereits in Deutschland an Steuerkanzleien, du kommst als Nächste:r dazu. Etwa einmal im Monat kommt das ganze deutsche Sales-Team für zwei Tage in Berlin zusammen. Deine Aufgaben als Account Executive – Steuerkanzleien: Du baust deine Pipeline auf: Rund 50 % kommen aus deinem eigenen Outbound – Cold Outreach, LinkedIn, Empfehlungen, Branchenevents –, die andere Hälfte aus qualifizierten Inbound-Leads. Du bleibst dran, auch wenn die ersten Antworten ein Nein sind. Du führst beratende Discovery-Gespräche mit Kanzleiinhaber:innen und Partner:innen, verstehst ihre Abläufe mit Mandanten und hinterfragst den Status quo. Du zeigst Pennylane im Kanzleialltag: Demos, die den konkreten Nutzen für Kanzlei und Mandanten zeigen, nicht die Feature-Liste. Du steuerst mehrstufige Deals mit mehreren Entscheider:innen bis zur Unterschrift – inklusive Einwand-Handling und Verhandlung. Du übergibst gewonnene Kanzleien an unser Customer-Success-Team in Berlin, das Onboarding und Betreuung übernimmt, baust dir Promoter-Kanzleien für Empfehlungen auf und hältst Salesforce und Forecast verlässlich aktuell. Woran du gemessen wirst: Du verantwortest den Umsatz aus Steuerkanzleien in deiner Region – gemessen an neu gewonnenen Kanzleien und an den Mandanten, die über diese Kanzleien aktiv auf Pennylane arbeiten. Du hältst deine Vertriebsziele konstant und baust den Marktanteil von Pennylane im Kanzleisegment deiner Region aus. Du bringst dein Wissen aus dem Markt in Playbook, Produkt-Feedback und die Go-to-Market-Strategie von Pennylane Deutschland ein. Dein Profil Du hast mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung im beratenden B2B-Vertrieb erklärungsbedürftiger Lösungen – mehrstufige Deals, mehrere Stakeholder – idealerweise mit SaaS, Kanzleisoftware oder Fintech und gern im Scale-up-Umfeld. Du verkaufst gern persönlich: Kundentermine vor Ort, Kanzleibesuche und Branchenevents in deiner Region gehören für dich dazu – nicht nur Telefon und Video-Call. Ein Plus: Du kennst den Markt der Steuerkanzleien oder das Accounting-/Fintech-Ökosystem (E-Rechnung, GoBD, Kanzleialltag) – oder bringst die Neugier mit, dich schnell einzuarbeiten. Du denkst unternehmerisch, hast den Drive, einen neuen Markt aufzubauen, und übernimmst Ownership für deine Zahlen, dein CRM und deinen Prozess. Du hörst aktiv zu, trittst bescheiden auf und baust Vertrauen zu traditionell arbeitenden Kanzleien auf – auf Augenhöhe mit Partner:innen und Steuerberater:innen. Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau, gutes Englisch für die Zusammenarbeit mit Paris – und du lebst in Berlin oder im Umkreis und kannst zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt starten. Was wir tun, um dein Arbeitsleben besser zu machen 📍 Remote: Homeoffice und Kundentermine in deiner Region. 🚀 Start zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt – du steigst in der Gründungsphase von Pennylane Deutschland ein. 🌴 30 Urlaubstage pro Jahr. 💵 Ein attraktives OTE-Paket: Fixgehalt plus ungedeckelter variabler Anteil, der quartalsweise ausgezahlt wird. 📈 Du erhältst Unternehmensanteile, um vom Erfolg mitzuprofitieren, den du gemeinsam mit uns aufbaust. 🏡 Du erhältst ein Budget für dein Homeoffice und eine monatliche Pauschale für einen Coworking-Space in deiner Stadt. 🇫🇷 Onboarding im Pariser HQ, regelmäßiger Austausch mit dem französischen Firms-Team und Zugang zu Busuu, um dein Englisch oder Französisch zu perfektionieren. 💻 Du erhältst die neueste Apple-Ausrüstung. 🎉 Wir legen Wert auf regelmäßige gemeinsame Veranstaltungen wie unsere Tech Days (alle 3 Monate) oder unser jährliches Firmenseminar – plus Team-Events in Berlin. Vielfalt und Inklusion Wir wissen, dass einige Menschen eher zögern, sich zu bewerben, wenn sie das Gefühl haben, nicht die gesamte Liste der Kriterien zu erfüllen. Wenn du unsicher bist, ermutigen wir dich, dich trotzdem zu bewerben: Wer weiß, vielleicht ist es der Beginn einer sinnvollen und langfristigen Zusammenarbeit. Wir möchten auch betonen, dass wir Vielfalt, Gleichheit und Inklusion voll und ganz befürworten und unser Bestes tun, um ein sicheres und integratives Umfeld zu schaffen. Wir verpflichten uns, gleiche Beschäftigungsmöglichkeiten unabhängig von Geschlecht, sexueller Orientierung, Herkunft, Behinderungen oder anderen Merkmalen, die dich ausmachen, zu gewährleisten. Im Gegenteil, Vielfalt macht uns zu einem noch besseren Arbeitsplatz. 🇫🇷 Données personnelles Pennylane traite vos données pour gérer votre candidature et évaluer votre adéquation au poste.
