title: Growth Engineer (Fullstack, Frontend-Focused)
description: Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)? Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy? Are our Engineering principles aligned with your vision? Then Pennylane is the right place for you ! Our vision We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones). We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business. About us Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!) In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to : 💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants 💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more... 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor . 🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe 🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings 🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France! Your impact Great growth experiences are built by great engineers. At Pennylane, Growth Engineering is about more than building landing pages or running experiments. It's about creating fast, reliable and seamless digital experiences that help entrepreneurs discover Pennylane and get started. As we expand across Europe, our website and acquisition journeys need to become more scalable, more flexible and more effective. We're looking for a Growth Engineer with strong frontend expertise to help us build the next generation of Pennylane's digital experiences. You'll join our Growth Engineering team and work closely with Thomas, our Growth Engineering Team Lead , within the Marketing Website squad. Your work will have a direct impact on how users discover, experience and adopt Pennylane. What you'll do Build great web experiences You'll develop and improve our public website and acquisition journeys, with a strong focus on frontend engineering. Build modern, responsive and high-performing interfaces using Vue.js and Nuxt.js. Develop and maintain fullstack features using Ruby on Rails. Improve website performance, accessibility and user experience. Build reusable components and scalable frontend solutions. Drive growth through engineering You'll work closely with Growth, Marketing and Data teams to turn business opportunities into technical solutions. Build and improve acquisition and registration funnels. Design and implement A/B tests and new user experiences. Improve conversion through technical experimentation. Develop features that support our international expansion, including localization and multilingual experiences. Connect systems and data You'll contribute to the technical foundations that power our growth initiatives. Build and maintain APIs and integrations between internal and external tools. Ensure reliable data flows across our digital ecosystem. Contribute to tracking implementations and data quality improvements. Work with Data teams to better understand user journeys and experiment results. Improve how we build You'll help us move fast without compromising engineering quality. Write clean, maintainable and well-tested code. Identify opportunities to simplify and automate workflows. Use AI-powered development tools when they bring real value. Take ownership of your projects, from technical design to production. Share knowledge and contribute to engineering best practices. Who are you? We're looking for an engineer who enjoys building products, solving technical challenges and seeing the impact of their work. Someone who combines strong engineering fundamentals with curiosity about user experience, experimentation and business impact. You don't need to be a marketing expert. But you should enjoy understanding why you're building something, not just how to build it. We'd love to meet you if... You have experience in software engineering, with strong frontend development skills. You're comfortable building modern web applications with Vue.js and/or Nuxt.js , or have strong experience with comparable frameworks and are ready to work with our stack. You're fluent in AI-assisted development : you work with coding agents, create custom skills and instructions, use worktrees to parallelize work and keep code quality high. You have fullstack experience and can contribute to backend development. Experience with Ruby on Rails is a strong plus. You enjoy taking ownership of technical projects from idea to production. You're comfortable collaborating with Engineering, Product, Growth, Marketing and Data teams. You're curious about experimentation, conversion optimization and how users interact with digital products. You're comfortable working in French and English. Bonus points if you have experience with: Web analytics and tracking tools such as Segment, Amplitude or Google Tag Manager. A/B testing and experimentation platforms. SEO, web performance or conversion optimization. API integrations and marketing automation. AI-assisted development workflows. Our tech stack Frontend: Vue.js, Nuxt.js, JavaScript Backend: Ruby on Rails Database: PostgreSQL Development: Git, GitHub You'll also have opportunities to work with analytics, tracking and experimentation tools depending on the projects. Why you'll love this role Real impact: Your work will directly influence how new customers discover and adopt Pennylane. Engineering challenges: You'll build scalable solutions, not just implement marketing requests. Ownership: You'll have the freedom to propose ideas, make technical decisions and drive projects forward. Cross-functional collaboration: You'll work at the intersection of Engineering, Growth, Marketing and Data. title: AI Developer
description: Salvo Software is a global technology company specializing in custom software development and advanced engineering solutions. With distributed teams across the US, LATAM, and India, we partner with clients to build high-performance, scalable systems that solve complex technical challenges. Our culture values innovation, ownership, and engineering excellence. We're growing our AI department and are looking for a hands-on AI Developer to help build it. Role Overview We are looking for an AI Developer to join and strengthen our AI department. Your core work will be building and operating LLM-powered systems: serving open-source models with Ollama and llama.cpp, building RAG pipelines, and developing MCP integrations that connect large language models to real tools and data. Solid DevOps fundamentals - Docker, CI/CD, Azure - support this work, but AI engineering is the heart of the role. You don't need to be a deep ML researcher. What matters is production-grade Python, strong fundamentals, and the aptitude to learn fast. You'll work closely with our engineering and product teams to take LLM-powered features from prototype to reliably deployed systems, with mentorship available as you ramp up in areas like RAG architecture, Kafka, and advanced MCP work. Key Responsibilities AI / LLM Engineering (core focus) Serve and operate open-source LLMs using Ollama and llama.cpp, locally and in on-prem environments. Build and maintain RAG pipelines: embeddings, vector databases, chunking strategies, and retrieval quality. Develop MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations connecting LLMs to internal tools and data sources. Build backend services in Python that power ML inference and AI-driven product features. Parse and process structured and semi-structured data (XML/XSD, Office document formats) as pipeline inputs. Grow into model optimization over time: quantization (GGUF), GPU/CUDA tuning, and offline/air-gapped deployments. DevOps & Infrastructure (supporting) Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for AI services (Azure DevOps preferred; GitHub Actions / GitLab CI also used). Deploy AI workloads to Microsoft Azure,AWS and containerize services with Docker. Automate operational tasks with Python, Bash and/or PowerShell scripting. Troubleshoot across the stack - dig into root causes rather than patching symptoms. Support event-driven architectures using Apache Kafka (producers/consumers). 3â5+ years engineering experience with production-level Python for building real services, LLM inference, RAG pipelines, and automated tooling. Hands-on LLM & AI integration serving models via Ollama/llama.cpp, implementing vector retrieval/RAG, and developing MCP integrations (GPU/CUDA tuning & model quantization nice to have). Cloud & Infrastructure expertise covering Azure/AWS deployments, Docker containerization, Linux/Windows admin, and CI/CD automation (Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions, or GitLab CI), with Terraform, Kubernetes, Kafka, or systems languages (Go, Rust, C++) as a plus. DevOps, Security & Operations awareness, including Git workflows, scripting (Python, Bash, PowerShell), observability tools (Prometheus/Grafana), DevSecOps, and compliance frameworks (SOC 2, ISO 27001, Zero Trust). Strong problem-solving & communication with a root-cause troubleshooting mindset, self-directed learning, strong ownership, and seamless remote/distributed team collaboration. Please mention the word **BREAKTHROUGHS** and tag RMjAuNTUuMTUuMjI3 when applying to show you read the job post completely (#RMjAuNTUuMTUuMjI3). This is a beta feature to avoid spam applicants. Companies can search these words to find applicants that read this and see they're human.

title: Principal Growth Marketing Strategist
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>Growth Marketing is the activation and delivery arm of GitLab marketing: campaigns, regional and field marketing, lifecycle and product led growth, marketing engineering and operations, corporate events including Transcend, partner marketing, community programs and Co-Create. If a program connects GitLab to a customer or a buyer, it lives here, and the team is accountable for pipeline, first orders, Flex conversion and expansion, and post sale adoption.</p> <p>As Principal Growth Marketing Strategist you work directly with the VP of Growth Marketing as a strategic partner and operator. You hold the whole picture of the engine: the goals every function has committed to, the budget and where it is moving, the strategic projects that do not fit cleanly inside any one function, and the decisions that are waiting on an answer. You keep that picture current, you act on it when the VP is engaged elsewhere, and you use it to move work faster.</p> <p>This is an individual contributor role at the Principal level. You do not manage a team. You manage outcomes across ten functions through influence, judgment and follow through, and you are trusted to speak for Growth Marketing in rooms the VP cannot be in. The people on the leadership team are senior, experienced marketers; they will work with you because you make them faster and sharper, not because of the title.</p> <p>You will be effective in this role if you have led marketing yourself at a senior level, understand how a modern B2B software company makes money, are curious and hands on with AI in your own work, and can move between a budget trade off, a partner negotiation, a pipeline review and a keynote plan in the same day without losing the thread.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Run Growth Marketing's operating rhythm: goals, business reviews, planning cycles and the metrics inspection behind them, so decisions get made, recorded and followed through.</li> <li>Track commitments across the leadership team between their 1:1s with the VP, so those conversations are about strategy rather than status.</li> <li>Own the strategic projects that matter to Growth Marketing and have no single functional home: scope them, find the owner or be the owner, and land them.</li> <li>Hold the budget picture across the team, prepare trade offs with a recommendation, and act within the authority the VP has delegated in writing.</li> <li>Represent Growth Marketing on the VP's behalf in pipeline reviews, cross functional planning and partner conversations; carry the position in and the decision out.</li> <li>Unblock functional leaders when the VP is engaged elsewhere, or stage the issue so it takes one conversation rather than three.</li> <li>Be a thinking partner to any functional leader who wants one, offered rather than assigned.</li> <li>Partner with marketing's AI Transformation Owner so AI adoption across Growth Marketing is visible, measured and moving.</li> <li>Prepare the VP for high stakes moments: executive updates, leadership material, keynotes, customer and partner meetings, with the numbers checked and the first draft written.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Extensive experience in B2B software marketing with senior leadership experience: you have owned a marketing function, a large program budget or a go to market motion, and you have been accountable for a pipeline or revenue number.</li> <li>Breadth across marketing. You have worked in or closely with demand and digital, field and events, lifecycle or product led growth, partner marketing and marketing operations, and you can hold a credible conversation with an expert in each.</li> <li>A track record of landing cross functional projects that nobody owned, through influence rather than authority, with executives, peers and individual contributors.</li> <li>Business fluency: you read a P&L, a pipeline report and a budget model comfortably, you understand consumption and subscription business models, and you can explain a trade off to a CFO in plain language.</li> <li>Program and operating rhythm experience: goal frameworks, business reviews, planning cycles, and the discipline to keep them honest without turning them into bureaucracy.</li> <li>Hands on AI fluency. You use AI tools daily in your own work, you have built or configured something with them, and you are curious about how they change the way a marketing organization operates. Prior experience in a chief of staff, strategy and operations, or business operations role is welcome but not required.</li> <li>Executive communication: concise writing, clear verbal briefs, comfort presenting to and being questioned by VPs and C level leaders, and the judgment to know what travels up and what does not.</li> <li>Discretion. You will handle confidential people, budget and strategy information every day.</li> <li>Familiarity with developer, DevOps or platform engineering audiences, or the ability to get there fast.</li> <li>The ability to use GitLab, and to travel occasionally for events and leadership offsites.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>Growth Marketing at GitLab is one integrated engine of roughly 100 people across ten functions, led by the VP of Growth Marketing and reporting into the Chief Product and Marketing Officer. The team runs Transcend, GitLab's flagship event program, the GitHub competitive motion, the regional and partner marketing engines in AMER, EMEA and APJ, the lifecycle and product led growth motions behind GitLab's self serve business, and marketing's AI transformation. The leadership team operates on a small set of shared principles: speed with quality, an ownership mindset, and customer outcomes. You can read more about <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/marketing/">how marketing operates at GitLab</a> in the handbook.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. This role defines how our communities grow and deliver value, building experiences that foster meaningful connections, sustained participation, and long-term engagement. This is an opportunity to build community as a growth practice, turning community relationships into impact supporting GitLab’s growth flywheel. </p> <h3><strong>What you'll do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Shape SELF's strategy and growth plans, building strategies that attract the right audiences and strengthen engagement and advocacy.</li> <li>Lead the programming and audience experience for SELF events and chapters. Ability to connect audience selection, programming, speaker engagement, and follow-up to member value and measurable outcomes.</li> <li>Familiarity with lifecycle marketing, marketing automation, CRM systems, web analytics, or campaign measurement.</li> <li>Strong cross-functional collaboration and writing skills, with the ability to communicate a program's value to different audiences.</li> <li>Ability to use member research, event feedback, engagement data, and marketing results to make decisions and improve programs.</li> <li>Sound judgment and the ability to balance ownership of SELF with marketing support for other community programs, working with operational partners on delivery.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the Team </strong></p> <p>The Growth Community Programs team supports GitLab’s growth flywheel, seeding tomorrow’s customers and activating today’s. title: Senior Field Marketer
description: WHO WE ARE Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vkpYpWfEK5s. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. ABOUT THE ROLE: Notion has a very successful "land and expand" business model; our customers start using Notion for free, upgrade over time as they expand their teams, and embrace increasingly sophisticated use cases. Often, these users and champions are different than the person who has enterprise purchasing authority. The Demand Generation team serves as a dot-connecter across sales, marketing, and operation teams to identify, engage, and convert decision makers at our target mid market and enterprise companies. In this role, you will partner with demand generation teammates and sales stakeholders to ideate and execute in-person events, designed to help open, accelerate, and close business. As a Field Marketing Manager, you will own and execute field events that are Notion-hosted, third party, co-partnered, and ancillary to third party events. This strategic position focuses on driving pipeline that meaningfully contribute to Notion's bottom line. This role can be based in either San Francisco or New York City. We work from our offices on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays (our Anchor Days) because we do our best thinking and building together in person. We’re looking for someone who’s excited to work alongside the team during those days. WHAT YOU'LL ACHIEVE: - Delight Notion customers and prospects, with a guest-first approach to creating field events and experiences that bring the Notion brand and product to life. - Own end-to-end planning, execution, and measurement of field programs to support our AMER Sales team - encompassing executive experiences, large-format educational events, trade shows, and co-sponsored activations with partners. - Manage all event logistics, production, venue sourcing, budget tracking, marketing campaigns, sales enablement, content development, and audience acquisition. - Leverage quantitative and qualitative insights to make recommendations on how we invest in field events to drive incremental business impact. - Partner closely with Sales and broader Marketing team to align events and audiences to objectives for top accounts and craft tailored programs that nurture those accounts - Partner with our Operation and BizTech teams to manage and better utilize our go-to-market systems SKILLS YOU'LL NEED TO BRING: - 8-12+ years of related marketing experience. - You don’t need to be an AI expert, but you’re curious and willing to adopt AI tools to work smarter and deliver better results. - You're a creative problem-solver who doesn't wait for a perfect playbook. You've built field events from scratch, and you're energized by figuring out what works in new territory. - You have a bias for action and experimentation. You'd rather test and learn than wait for consensus, and you know how to balance scrappiness with strategic thinking. - You're a strong cross-functional collaborator. You know how to work with sales, ops, and creative teams — and you can align people around a shared goal without needing authority to do it. - You're pipeline-obsessed. You understand how your programs connect to revenue and can speak credibly about pipeline contribution, not just top-of-funnel metrics. NICE TO HAVES: - Experience in a fast-paced, B2B tech environment - You're a Notion user and understand our value to businesses - Salesforce, Marketo experience Notion is committed to providing highly competitive cash compensation, equity, and benefits. The compensation offered for this role will be based on multiple factors such as location, the role’s scope and complexity, and the candidate’s experience and expertise, and may vary from the range provided below. For roles based in San Francisco or New York City, the estimated base salary range for this role is $175,000-$200,000 per year. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirement — when that’s the case, we'll say so explicitly in the qualifications. People who thrive here don’t treat AI as a novelty. They use it to think better, and make their work easier for others to build on. EQUAL OPPORTUNITY & ACCOMMODATIONS We hire talented people from a wide range of backgrounds. If you’re excited about this role but don’t meet every bullet, we still encourage you to apply. title: GTM, Strategic Planning
description: Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search — all deeply integrated and designed for growth. We're building the best developer platform to power the next generation of software companies, and our go-to-market team is scaling fast to match. We're looking for a lead in Go-To-Market Strategic Planning, to shape how Supabase's GTM engine runs. This is a high-leverage, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution. You'll work directly with Success, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Partnerships and Product to build the systems, processes, and insights that help our go-to-market teams move faster and smarter. WHAT YOU'LL DO - Own the end-to-end GTM Strategic Planning, covering territory design, segmentation design, target planning and GTM capacity planning. - Build and maintain a single source of truth for planning data across HubSpot, BigQuery and Hex. - Translate company priorities into field actions through designing the planning strategy and seeing it through to execution. - Partner with Sales Leadership to design and iterate on coverage models, segmentation, and team structures that reflect how developers actually buy. - Define and track the metrics that matter, and surface insights that drive action, not just reporting. - Lead the Strategic Planning roadmap: guide and lead in tooling investments and evaluate new systems and processes against real business needs. - Work cross-functionally with talent acquisition, ensuring GTM and territory models stay aligned. - Collaborate with GTM Engineering on automations and data pipelines so that your strategy translates into working systems, not just slide decks. WE'LL EXPECT YOU TO - Operate with high ownership. You set your own agenda, escalate when needed, and don't wait to be asked. - Work asynchronously and document clearly. We're a globally distributed team and writing is how we think. - Bridge strategy and execution. From drafting segmentation approaches in Google Docs to using SQL to monitor its effectiveness. - Build for scale without over-engineering. Simple systems that work beat perfect systems that don't ship. - Stay close to the customer. Developers are our buyers, and understanding how they discover, adopt, and expand is core to everything you'll do. YOU MIGHT BE A FIT IF YOU - Have 6+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Strategy Consulting, GTM Strategy, or Sales Operations at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company. - Are fluent in the GTM stack: HubSpot, BigQuery, and Hightouch. - Can write SQL comfortably and aren't afraid to get into the data yourself before asking an analyst. - Have experience designing or overhauling sales processes, forecasting cadences, or territory models in a high-growth environment. - Understand product-led growth motions: PLS, usage-based triggers, and how PLG data flows into commercial pipelines. - Thrive with autonomy and are energized by building things that didn't exist before you joined. - Communicate with clarity across Finance, Sales, Success, Partnerships, Engineering, and Marketing without losing nuance. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when. - Professional Development Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth. ABOUT THE TEAM Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love. - ~400 team members - 60+ countries - 20+ languages spoken - Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F) - 540,000+ community members We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

title: Corporate Development Director
location: Remote Ireland; Remote, France; Remote, Germany; Remote, Israel; Remote, Netherlands; Remote, Spain; Remote, United Kingdom
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2 id="an-overview-of-this-role" data-lfile-container="21ea07e5-ded4-47e8-ad92-4ca7b7d6be35" data-pm-slice="1 1 []">An overview of this role</h2> <p>As the Corporate Development Director, you'll help influence how GitLab invests to win: what we build, what we buy, where we partner, and what we should not pursue. This role sits within the Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships.</p> <p>This role straddles strategy and M&A engagements. You'll lead research that frames GitLab's options: mapping the markets in and around our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, testing where we have a right to win, and turning that into clear recommendations for the executive team. When the answer is to acquire, you'll drive the deal process end to end, from outreach through close and integration.</p> <p>Success here is not measured by deal count. It looks like sharper strategic choices: a well-reasoned point of view on our priority markets, investment theses that product and executive leaders rely on, acquisitions that speed up the roadmap when buying is the right answer, and an educated no when it isn't. You'll own the wider market perspective rather than individual product categories, and work with the team's Analyst on the research behind it.</p> <h2 id="what-youll-do">What you'll do</h2> <h3 id="strategy-and-research">Strategy and research</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Own the wider market view.</strong> Research the broader market GitLab competes in, beyond specific product categories: competitive dynamics, AI-native entrants, technology shifts and where value is moving. Collaborate with the team's Analyst on the research and turn the findings into a clear point of view on where GitLab should play.</li> <li><strong>Build an investment thesis for each focus area.</strong> Work with Product and Engineering leaders to define the problems worth solving, the capabilities GitLab needs, and what it would cost in time and money to get there on our own.</li> <li><strong>Own the competitive and landscape view.</strong> Maintain market maps and a current read on GitLab's competitors: their strategy, product direction, positioning, pricing, and M&A and funding activity. Produce competitor analyses that show where we lead, where we're exposed and how rivals are likely to move. Flag shifts by competitors, hyperscalers and AI labs that change our options, and bring the implications to Product and the executive team.</li> <li><strong>Define where GitLab should not play.</strong> Identify adjacencies that dilute focus and markets where the economics or competition work against us. Make the case for a no with the same rigor as a yes.</li> </ul> <h3 id="build-buy-or-partner">Build, buy or partner</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Run the build, buy, partner analysis.</strong> For each strategic gap, compare the options side by side on speed, cost, risk, control and strategic fit, and bring a clear recommendation.</li> <li><strong>Deliver strategic clarity to</strong> <strong>executives and the Board.</strong> Produce short strategy memos/decks and business cases that set out the decision, the trade-offs and what we give up with each path.</li> <li><strong>Feed company strategy and planning.</strong> Bring an outside-in view of the market and the inorganic options available into annual and long-range planning.</li> <li><strong>Work hand in hand with Strategic Partnerships.</strong> When partnering is the right answer, frame the opportunity and hand it to the partnership owner with a clear thesis. When it isn't, explain why.</li> </ul> <h3 id="deal-execution-and-integration">Deal execution and integration</h3> <ul> <li><strong>Own end-to-end deal process management.</strong> Validate target fit against GitLab's our target profile, product roadmap and other criteria, and build the acquisition rationale and business case. Drive our M&A process from intro call through the various steps through to closing and integration.</li> <li><strong>Evaluate the deal.</strong> Develop valuation, commercial integrity assessment, impact on GitLab's business and provide negotiations assistance to the VP and the executive team.</li> <li><strong>Lead cross-functional diligence.</strong> Run pre-LOI validation and diligence across Product, Engineering, Security, Finance, Legal and People, and communicate findings clearly.</li> <li><strong>Drive deal documents with Legal.</strong> Prepare NDAs, LOIs and purchase agreements with GitLab Legal and outside counsel.</li> <li><strong>Own integration outcomes.</strong> Lead post-acquisition integration as the DRI, measured against the roadmap and business goals in the business case. Bring lessons learned back into the strategy work.</li> <li><strong>Build the external network.</strong> Maintain relationships with founders, executives, investors, bankers and advisors that bring us early insight and pipeline.</li> </ul> <h2 id="what-youll-bring">What you'll bring</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Strategy and deal experience.</strong> 8+ years across corporate development, corporate strategy, strategy consulting or technology investing, including 5+ years leading acquisitions end to end in enterprise software.</li> <li><strong>Structured strategic thinking.</strong> You form a point of view from incomplete information, test it against data, and change your mind when the evidence says so. You're as comfortable recommending that we stay out of a market as that we enter it.</li> <li><strong>Market research depth.</strong> Skilled in market sizing, competitive analysis and landscape mapping, and in turning research into a recommendation, not a report.</li> <li><strong>Deal craft.</strong> Skilled in valuation, financial modeling, deal structuring, negotiation and integration planning, with experience across varied consideration structures.</li> <li><strong>Technical fluency.</strong> A working understanding of software development, DevSecOps and the AI landscape, enough to hold substantive conversations with product and engineering leaders about roadmaps and architecture.</li> <li><strong>Clear executive communication.</strong> You write short, decision-ready updates and present trade-offs plainly to executives and the Board, in an async-first environment.</li> <li><strong>Influence without authority.</strong> You build trust across Product, Engineering, Finance and Legal and move decisions forward across functions.</li> <li><strong>Ownership with collaboration.</strong> You own the strategic view and the recommendation, and partner closely with the team's Analyst on research and analysis.</li> <li><strong>Preferred:</strong> familiarity with the DevSecOps, security, AI and open source ecosystems.</li> <li>You value the <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/all-remote/" target="_blank">all remote</a> lifestyle and share our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/values/" target="_blank">values</a>.</li> </ul> <h2 id="about-the-team">About the team</h2> <p>The Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships team helps GitLab decide how to grow beyond what we build on our own. We own inorganic strategy: acquisitions, strategic partnerships with hyperscalers and AI labs, and the research that tells us which to pursue and which to pass on.</p> <p>We work across Product, Engineering, Finance, Legal and the executive group. We set direction and do the detailed work ourselves, with a high degree of ownership and transparency in a fully remote, asynchronous environment.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><h4><strong>How GitLab Supports Full-Time Employees</strong></h4> <ul> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/">Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/#flexible-paid-time-off-pto">Flexible Paid Time Off </a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/company/culture/inclusion/tmrg-tmag/">Team Member Resource Groups</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/stock-options/">Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan</a></li> <li><a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/">Growth and Development Fund</a></li> <li><a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave">Parental Leave</a> </li> </ul> <p>Please note that we welcome interest from candidates with varying levels of experience; many successful candidates do not meet every single requirement. Additionally, studies have shown that people from <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/company/culture/inclusion/#examples-of-select-underrepresented-groups">underrepresented groups</a> are less likely to apply to a job unless they meet every single qualification. If you're excited about this role, please apply and allow our recruiters to assess your application.</p> <hr> <p><strong>Country Hiring Guidelines: </strong>GitLab hires new team members in countries around the world. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after start

title: AI Solution Architect (m/w/d)
description: Als IT-Dienstleister treiben wir die Digitalisierung des öffentlichen Sektors voran und schaffen echten Mehrwert für Millionen Menschen in Deutschland. Wir können vieles richtig gut, aber eben noch nicht alles. Darum suchen wir immer wieder neue Kolleg:innen, die mit ihren Ideen, ihrem Können und Engagement etwas bewegen wollen. Du verbindest fundiertes Know-how in ML Engineering, RAG-Architekturen und MLOps, um KI-Lösungen produktionsreif, skalierbar und sicher umzusetzen. Dabei arbeitest Du eng mit technischen Expert:innen, Fachbereichen und Entscheidungsträgern zusammen und trägst maßgeblich dazu bei, innovative KI-Lösungen erfolgreich zu etablieren. Deine Aufgaben: Entwurf und Weiterentwicklung der KI-/ML-Gesamtarchitektur als Enterprise-KI-Plattform mit Schwerpunkt Microsoft Azure Technische Leitung von ML-Pipeline-Projekten, insbesondere in den Bereichen Training, Deployment, Monitoring und Drift Detection Konzeption und Optimierung von RAG-Architekturen, beispielsweise hinsichtlich Chunking, Retrieval, Guardrails und Context Orchestration Definition und Weiterentwicklung von MLOps-Strategien einschließlich CI/CD für Modelle, Experiment-Tracking und Model Registry Technische Führung und Koordination interdisziplinärer Teams aus ML/AI Engineers, LLM Engineers und MLOps Engineers Beratung interner und externer Stakeholder zu KI-Architekturen sowie Präsentation technischer Konzepte gegenüber IT-Leitung und Fachbereichen DAS IST UNS WICHTIG Fundierte Erfahrung mit cloudbasierten KI-/ML-Lösungen, idealerweise auf Microsoft Azure, insbesondere Azure Machine Learning und Azure OpenAI Service. Kenntnisse weiterer Cloud- und AI-Services sind von Vorteil. Praktische Erfahrung mit MLOps-Konzepten und entsprechenden Werkzeugen wie MLflow, Kubeflow oder Azure ML Pipelines. Erfahrung im Aufbau von RAG-Architekturen, Prompt Engineering und im Umgang mit Vektordatenbanken. Kenntnisse in der Integration und Orchestrierung von Sprachmodellen, idealerweise mit Frameworks wie LangChain oder LlamaIndex. Praktische Erfahrung mit mindestens zwei gängigen Machine-Learning-Frameworks, beispielsweise scikit-learn, PyTorch oder TensorFlow. Erfahrung im Aufbau von Enterprise-Architekturen in Cloud-Umgebungen. Kenntnisse in angrenzenden Bereichen wie Datenplattformen, Containerisierung, Container-Orchestrierung, Infrastructure as Code und Observability sind von Vorteil, beispielsweise mit Databricks, Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake, Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana oder Application Insights. description: Hol' dir den Kick als DocCheck Software Engineer – AI-Assisted Development (m/w/d) Seit Jahrzehnten ist DocCheck im DACH-Raum und darüber hinaus eine bekannte Healthcare-Größe. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move from strategy to execution without heavy oversight.</p> <p>This role reports to the Vice President, Enablement & AI.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li><strong>AI Enablement Roadmap:</strong> Own and continuously evolve the roadmap for AI-driven enablement initiatives, prioritizing based on field impact, feasibility, and alignment with broader Enterprise AI team and strategy..</li> <li><strong>AI Field Use Cases:</strong> Identify, scope, and execute on high-value AI use cases for the field (e.g., deal support, prospecting, content generation, guided selling, skills, change management), working with stakeholders to define success criteria and measure impact.</li> <li><strong>AI Field Champions: </strong>build relationships with champions in the field organization to activate power-usage and drive peer-led adoption; track this adoption (e.g., usage, proficiency, behavior change) with our AI Ops Specialist and Enablement Analyst.</li> </ul> <ul> <li><strong>Ops Transformation Plan:</strong> Design and drive the operational plan that turns AI pilots into scaled, repeatable processes, coordinating across enablement, ops, and technical teams to remove execution bottlenecks.</li> <li><strong>AI Governance:</strong> Influence and lead governance standards for AI tool adoption in the field, including data usage, risk review, tool vetting, and alignment with company-wide AI policy.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Mid-Senior Experience:</strong> Several years of experience in enablement, sales operations, or a related GTM function, with a track record of owning initiatives end-to-end.</li> <li><strong>AI Solutions Experience:</strong> Direct experience evaluating, piloting, or deploying AI tools or solutions in a business context, with a solid technical understanding of how they work and where they add value. Act as the field's primary advocate for AI tools (e.g., AI-assisted prospecting, call intelligence, forecasting copilots, RFP/proposal generation).</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Fluency:</strong> Proven ability to work closely with product and engineering teams, translating field needs into technical requirements and vice versa.</li> <li><strong>Self-Sufficiency:</strong> Comfortable operating with significant autonomy — able to define scope, structure ambiguous problems, and drive work forward without needing detailed direction.</li> <li><strong>Organization & Execution:</strong> Strong project management instincts; able to manage multiple workstreams (roadmap, use cases, ops transformation, governance) in parallel without dropping details.</li> <li><strong>Innovative Mindset:</strong> A builder's orientation toward new technology — curious about what's possible, willing to experiment, and able to separate genuine opportunity from hype.</li> <li><strong>Enablement/Sales Background:</strong> Familiarity with field or sales enablement motions (onboarding, tool adoption, content, coaching) and how AI can realistically augment them.</li> <li><strong>GitLab Values Alignment:</strong> Ability to work in an all-remote, asynchronous environment, leaning heavily on transparency and collaboration as defined in the GitLab Handbook.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Enablement & AI function is part of the CRO organization. The Associate Renewals Manager works under the general direction of Senior Renewals Managers and their manager, following specific instructions and frameworks in day-to-day work. Solutions and outputs are reviewed by more senior team members and/or the direct manager.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Manage an assigned portfolio of customer renewals remote work best practices.</li> <li>Growth mindset and sense of ownership — proactively seeks out ways to learn and improve, and takes action rather than waiting for direction.</li> <li>Strong attention to detail and organizational skills; comfortable managing many renewals at once.</li> <li>Clear written and verbal communication skills.</li> <li>Ability to follow defined processes and frameworks while flagging exceptions appropriately.</li> <li>Collaborative mindset and openness to feedback and coaching from senior teammates and manager.</li> <li><span class="s1">The ability to travel for events such as trainings, team offsites, customer meetings, etc.</span></li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The Renewals team focuses on protecting and growing GitLab's In this role, you’ll deliver features and improvements in well-scoped areas, learn the broader architecture, and contribute to reliability, observability, and operational readiness.</p> <p>In your first year, you’ll take clear ownership of specific components or features (for example, parts of the SDLC indexing pipeline or query paths). You’ll help reduce single points of failure with better tests and runbooks, and you’ll help the team ship analytical services that are easier to maintain and evolve over time.</p> <p><strong><strong of the GitLab platform, working in areas that touch GitLab Rails, the Data Insights Platform (Siphon, NATS, ClickHouse), and GitLab Duo Agent Platform.</li> <li value="3">Contribute to system design discussions by proposing options, raising questions, and documenting decisions, with a focus on reliability, scalability, and maintainability for analytical graph workloads.</li> <li value="4">Improve the operational maturity of the service by adding or enhancing metrics, logging, runbooks, alerts, and small readiness tasks, and by participating in on-call rotation as appropriate for your level and experience.</li> <li value="5">Collaborate asynchronously with product, data, infrastructure, security, and AI counterparts to clarify requirements, align on scope, and ship features safely for customers and sustainably for the team.</li> <li value="6">Use AI-assisted development workflows responsibly (for example, using Knowledge Graph-backed agents and internal Duo tooling), and share what works with the team while keeping a strong focus on code quality and correctness.</li> <li value="7">Participate in code reviews, knowledge-sharing sessions, and pairing to both learn from others and help maintain consistent standards across the codebase.</li> <li value="8">Contribute across the stack when needed, including occasional Ruby work for Rails integration and authorization paths, or small frontend changes related to Knowledge Graph features (for example, Software Architecture Map UI plumbing).</li> <li value="8">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll bring</strong></strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Professional experience building and maintaining backend systems in production, with an understanding of reliability, maintainability, and how to support services over time (for example, incident response and follow-ups).</li> <li value="2">Proficiency in at least one modern backend language and strong interest in Rust, with either prior Rust experience or clear evidence you can ramp quickly and deliver in a Rust-first, performance-sensitive codebase.</li> <li value="3">Some exposure to distributed data or analytics systems (for example, OLAP databases, Kafka- or NATS-style messaging, or change data capture (CDC) pipelines), or strong motivation to develop those skills in this role.</li> <li value="4">Interest in graph data modeling and query patterns (property graphs, multi-step (n-hop) traversals, aggregations), and willingness to learn the tools and concepts used in Knowledge Graph over time.</li> <li value="5">Practical experience (or strong interest) using AI tools in day-to-day development, along with a thoughtful approach to validating outputs and integrating AI into your workflow.</li> <li value="6">A language-agnostic mindset and evidence that you can pick up new languages and frameworks as needed (for example, Ruby, Go, or TypeScript/Vue where the work touches adjacent systems).</li> <li value="7">Solid fundamentals in system design for your level, including the ability to reason about trade-offs, ask good questions, and align your implementation work with documented architectural decisions.</li> <li value="8">Comfort working in a low-process, high-ownership environment where you take responsibility for your work, refine problem statements with teammates, and communicate progress clearly in writing across time zones in an all-remote team.</li> </ul> <p><strong><strong class="textBold">About the team</strong></strong></p> <p>GitLab Orbit sits within the Data Engineering organization. We work closely with partners across AI (Duo Agent Platform), analytics, infrastructure and delivery, and security because our work spans many parts of the platform.</p> <p>We collaborate asynchronously rather than following a feature factory model. collaborative code review processes.</li> <li>Experience using artificial intelligence coding agents and reviewing their output, or an interest in building these skills in a complex monorepo.</li> logs, traces, dashboards, and alerts.</li> <li>Contributing to a modular monolith, bounded context, shared component, or independently operated service.</li> </ul> <div customer needs.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Practical understanding of Git, common branching strategies, and modern software development lifecycles.</li> <li value="2">Working knowledge of continuous integration, continuous deployment, and DevSecOps practices.</li> <li value="3">Experience partnering with customers to define business outcomes and translate them into actionable success plans, key goals, and measures.</li> <li value="4">Background in customer success, post-sales, or professional services roles focused on adoption, retention, and satisfaction.</li> <li value="5">Ability to manage a portfolio of customers, including handling escalations and coordinating across Support, Product Management, Sales, and Professional Services.</li> maintain and advocate for these standards through code review</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>3-5 years of professional experience in GTM analytics, data science, or a similar technical role</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to translate ambiguous business problems into clear, measurable questions and communicate technical concepts effectively to non-technical stakeholders.</li> <li>Experience with experimentation and causal inference (A/B testing, power analysis, quasi-experimental methods) and with statistical and machine learning methods such as regression, classification, clustering, and survival analysis</li> <li>Deep, hands-on understanding of SQL in cloud data warehouses (like Snowflake SQL), including working with product usage and event data, and in business intelligence tools (Looker, Tableau, Hex, or similar)</li> <li>Experience using Python for statistical modeling, machine learning, and production data science. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Director, Analytics Engineering, you'll lead a team of 8 and report to the VP of Data & Insights. You set direction across the data organization, stay close enough to the work to guide technical decisions credibly, and partner with Data Engineering, Data Science, IT, and business leaders.<br>You will have three mandates:</p> <ol> <li><strong>Build trusted, AI-ready self-service.</strong> Deliver a semantic model that answers business questions correctly, with the telemetry, evals, and model flexibility to prove it and keep costs in check.</li> <li><strong>Set the strategy for how GitLab accesses data.</strong> Own the data models, BI tools, and AI access patterns (Claude, MCP servers, Slack agents) that put trusted data in everyone's hands.</li> <li><strong>Build data applications the whole company relies on.</strong> Ship production-grade apps that combine trusted data, APIs, and AI to answer questions dashboards can't.</li> </ol> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Build and own a trusted semantic model, with governed metrics and business definitions, that answers business questions consistently across every tool</li> <li>Build evals and ground-truth datasets that measure answer quality, and use them to drive improvements and catch regressions</li> <li>Instrument telemetry to see who uses the semantic model and AI tools, what they ask, and where they get stuck</li> <li>Build a model-selection harness so GitLab can route work across LLMs and stay flexible on cost and quality</li> <li>Own data modeling and curated datasets for self-service, with the ownership, data contracts, testing, and documentation that make them AI-ready</li> <li>Define the AI data access strategy: when to use BI, Claude, MCP servers, or Slack agents, with the governance and security to keep access trusted and reliable</li> <li>Own the enterprise BI and self-service tools strategy (e.g., Tableau, Omni), including evaluation, adoption, and cost</li> <li>Build self-service capabilities, such as Claude skills, documentation, and guided workflows, that help people find and use data on their own</li> <li>Build and own company-wide data applications, from Claude-built single-page apps to apps inside BI tools, that combine Snowflake data, API calls, AI-powered deep dives, and write-back to Postgres or Snowflake</li> <li>Set engineering standards for data apps (security, authentication, testing, deployment, and monitoring) so they're reliable at company scale</li> <li>Set a long-range roadmap tied to company strategy, and a lightweight operating model that balances urgent stakeholder needs with investment in reusable data products and tech-debt reduction</li> <li>Hire, coach, and retain a high-performing team of 8: build career paths, develop leaders, distribute ownership, and recognize great work</li> <li>Act as customer zero for GitLab and GitLab Duo in data workflows, sharing feedback with Product and Engineering</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>12+ years in analytics engineering, data engineering, or BI, including 5+ years leading teams and 2+ years managing managers or senior leads</li> <li>Deep expertise in data modeling and semantic layers (e.g., dbt Semantic Layer, Snowflake semantic views, LookML, Cube), and expert dbt, including testing and CI/CD across a multi-team project</li> <li>Hands-on experience building LLM-powered data access (text-to-SQL, agents, MCP servers), including evals and telemetry for answer quality, and advanced use of AI coding agents such as Claude Code</li> <li>Expert SQL and strong Snowflake experience; working knowledge of Python</li> <li>Strong data governance experience: data quality, lineage, certified datasets, and access controls (RBAC, row access and masking policies)</li> <li>Track record of leading cross-functional data initiatives from strategy through adoption and measurable business impact, including enterprise BI and self-service at scale</li> <li>Systems thinker who sees how models, pipelines, and architecture decisions connect, and designs for second-order effects</li> <li>Exceptional communicator who writes clear technical specs, sets a clear vision, makes trade-offs visible, and influences executives and peers across the company</li> <li>Pragmatic in ambiguity: makes sound decisions on emerging technology and ships the right next version rather than waiting for the ideal end state</li> <li>Able to use GitLab, thrive in an all-remote, asynchronous company, model GitLab's remote working competencies, and work in line with GitLab's values</li> </ul> <h2><strong>Nice to Have</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience with LLM routing or gateway tools and managing model costs</li> <li>Experience with Tableau, Omni, or a BI platform migration</li> <li>Experience with web app development (e.g., React, TypeScript) and Postgres</li> <li>Experience owning finance or revenue-critical data (e.g., ARR, consumption) where accuracy and auditability are non-negotiable</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>Analytics Engineering makes GitLab's data trusted, easy to find, and ready for anyone to use, whether they ask a dashboard, Claude, or a Slack agent. We own the curated data models, the semantic layer, the self-service tools, and the data applications that let teams answer their own questions.</p> <p>AI is changing how people get to data. Questions that once went through an analyst now go straight to AI tools, so the answers are only as good as the data models and business definitions behind them. Our job is to make those answers correct, consistent, and measurable.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. <li>Experience supporting software that customers run themselves, or working through the self-managed upgrade challenge.</li> <li>Experience leading backend engineering teams that own production communicating clearly in writing in an asynchronous, handbook-first company.</li> <li>Experience leading globally distributed remote teams.</li> <li>Experience with Redis, ClickHouse, OpenSearch, More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As Director, Product Management: Agentic Software Delivery, you'll own one of GitLab's most strategic sections, spanning Continuous Integration, Artifact Management, Continuous Deployment, and Observability. You'll lead senior and principal product managers and be accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue across build, package, deploy, and monitor. Today, these are separate stages with a human making the call at each handoff. As agents take on more coding, pipeline, and deployment work, you'll set the three-year vision for how much of that judgment the system can make safely and how quickly a production signal can turn into a fix without waiting for a human to notice it first. You'll define how customers move from today's manual checkpoints toward agent-driven software delivery at a pace that fits their risk tolerance. leaders, and give customers a credible path for managing software delivery at scale.</p> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Own the strategy, three-year vision, and business outcomes for GitLab's Agentic Software Delivery section, with a clear point of view on how artificial intelligence is changing software delivery.</li> <li value="2">Lead and develop senior and principal product standards, and operating rhythm that support consistent, high-quality product decisions without unnecessary escalation.</li> <li value="4">Own section-level key performance indicators and adoption funnels, using the results to reallocate investment or stop work that isn't paying off.</li> <li value="5">Evaluate major strategic bets, partnerships, and build, buy, or partner decisions, and develop the business cases that support them.</li> <li value="6">Partner with Engineering leadership on platform investment, architectural direction, and trade-offs across the section, while connecting build, package, deploy, and monitor into one coherent customer experience.</li> <li value="7">Drive pricing, packaging, go-to-market strategy, migration, and adoption with Product Marketing, Sales, Pricing, Customer Success, and Solutions Engineering across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="8">Represent the section with GitLab's senior leadership, key enterprise customers, partners, and industry audiences, while modeling AI-native product management across discovery, synthesis, prototyping, roadmap exploration, and concept development.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience leading product managers, including developing senior and principal talent, hiring, and addressing performance directly.</li> <li value="2">A track record of owning a portfolio across multiple product areas and being accountable for adoption, retention, and revenue, not only roadmap delivery.</li> <li value="3">Product management depth in one or more relevant areas, such as continuous integration and continuous delivery pipelines, artifact or package management, release management, or observability.</li> <li value="4">Sound judgment about where to invest and where to stop, including experience making and defending build, buy, or partner decisions with a business case.</li> <li value="5">Technical fluency to work with engineers and architects on pipeline design, artifact workflows, deployment strategies, and observability signals such as logs, metrics, and traces.</li> <li value="6">Experience shaping pricing and packaging for technical products across free, commercial, and enterprise offerings.</li> <li value="7">Experience working with technical customers in developer tools, DevOps, or software delivery environments where engineers and engineering leaders are primary users.</li> <li value="8">Executive-level communication and influence.</li> <li value="9">Practical use of AI tools in product management workflows, along with a thoughtful view of how AI and agentic workflows are changing software delivery. We welcome candidates whose experience may come from different but transferable product and leadership paths.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The team brings together senior product leaders across GitLab's software delivery platform and works closely with Engineering, Design, and go-to-market partners so customers experience these capabilities as one connected system. The team helps customers manage today's delivery complexity while shaping how AI-powered and AI-native workflows influence the next generation of software delivery. You'll connect reliability, scalability, and operability with the commercial decisions that make these platforms sustainable businesses.</p> <p>Your scope spans both platforms, not a single feature roadmap. On GitLab.com, you'll guide growth through better customer isolation and additional cells, alongside rate limits, usage limits, and monetization. On GitLab Dedicated, you'll help scale it to hundreds of customers through automation, customer self-service, and closer alignment with GitLab's latest releases. You'll balance customer needs with operating costs and gross margin.</p> <p>This director-level role starts as an individual contributor. It's remote and open to candidates based in the United States or Canada, with no specific time zone preference.</p> <h2><strong>What You'll Do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Set the product strategy and roadmap across GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated, connecting platform capabilities to customer and business outcomes.</li> <li>Drive improvements in platform reliability, scalability, and operability, including better separation between customers and expansion of GitLab.com's cell-based architecture.</li> <li>Define GitLab.com's rate limits, usage limits, and related monetization approach.</li> <li>Scale GitLab Dedicated through maintenance-window automation and other operational improvements, while controlling costs and improving gross margin.</li> <li>Expand customer self-service through Switchboard, giving customers tools to monitor, observe, and operate their Dedicated tenants.</li> <li>Guide capabilities such as customer-initiated disaster recovery and geographic redundancy, and enable earlier access to beta features on GitLab Dedicated.</li> <li>Reduce the delay between GitLab releases and their availability on Dedicated.</li> <li>Own the business side of the portfolio as well as the technical product direction, developing profit and loss (P&L) ownership for both platforms and helping establish GitLab.com as a P&L business.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What You'll Bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience leading a product portfolio at director level or with comparable scope, setting direction across multiple related products rather than a single roadmap.</li> connect product decisions to commercial outcomes, including monetization, operating costs, and gross margin.</li> <li>Experience translating complex platform challenges into product priorities and working across teams to deliver them.</li> <li>The ability to lead through product direction and influence in a director-level individual contributor role.</li> </ul> <p>Direct ownership of a product P&L is particularly valuable. Experience in an organization actively adopting artificial intelligence (AI) would also be helpful.</p> <h2><strong>About the Team</strong></h2> <p>The SaaS platform portfolio brings together GitLab.com and GitLab Dedicated. The work spans shared-platform growth, single-tenant operations, and the tools customers use to manage their environments. The challenge is to improve the customer experience and platform capabilities while building a scalable, financially sustainable operating model for each offering.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Director, Social Media, you'll lead GitLab's global social media strategy and help people understand how GitLab is co-creating the future of software development. The role shapes how GitLab shows up across social channels, connecting our company, product, and employer stories, to build meaningful engagement with customers, users, contributors, candidates, and industry audiences. Expect to set clear priorities, guide execution, and use insights to strengthen GitLab's voice and business impact. You'll own the outcomes of GitLab's social function — strategy, budget, team development, tooling, and results — and serve as GitLab's senior-most voice on social strategy with executive stakeholders.</p> <p>This is a player-coach role. You'll set the strategy and stay close enough to the work to write, build, and ship alongside the team. Two Social Media Managers report to the head of corporate communication and work with you on a dotted-line basis. You'll set their strategic direction, raise the editorial and craft bar, and develop them as practitioners, including goal-setting, feedback, and career development in partnership with their manager. Influence matters in this role, which is why it calls for someone who has already led and grown social practitioners. </p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Own the performance of GitLab's social function and its contribution to marketing and business goals.</li> <li>Lead GitLab's global organic social media strategy, channel plans, and editorial priorities.</li> <li>Own GitLab's YouTube strategy end to end — channel architecture, programming and series development, long- and short-form video, packaging (titles, thumbnails, metadata), search and recommendation optimization, and subscriber and watch-time growth.</li> <li>Partner with Growth Marketing on paid social, including briefing creative, aligning organic and paid on shared audiences and messaging, informing boosting and amplification decisions, and connecting paid performance back to organic strategy.</li> <li>Develop clear, audience-focused campaigns that support company, product, brand, and talent goals.</li> <li>Guide content planning and publishing across social channels while maintaining a consistent GitLab voice.</li> <li>Own the social media budget, tooling stack, and agency, freelance, and production partner relationships.</li> <li>Partner with teams across Marketing, Communications, Product, Sales, Talent Acquisition, and other functions to plan and deliver social programs.</li> <li>Build processes that support effective collaboration in GitLab's all-remote, asynchronous environment.</li> <li>Use social listening, audience insights, and performance data to improve content and inform broader marketing decisions.</li> <li>Lead the measurement framework for social — KPIs, dashboards, and reporting cadence — and report performance and learnings to marketing and executive leadership.</li> <li>Partner with DevRel on community engagement to help GitLab participate in relevant industry conversations with a clear, useful point of view.</li> <li>Build and run creator, influencer, and advocacy programs, including developer creators, GitLab community contributors, and team member advocacy.</li> <li>Own GitLab's employee advocacy program — grow participation across Marketing, Sales, Engineering, and Talent, equip team members with content worth sharing, and measure reach, engagement, and contribution to brand and talent goals. Partner with Communications and Talent Acquisition on enablement, and manage the advocacy platform and its adoption.</li> <li>Support executive and expert social presence, partnering with Communications to help GitLab leaders and technical experts show up credibly on social, including constructive conversations with C-suite executives about proposed content.</li> <li>Apply AI tools thoughtfully across the social workflow to help GitLab model what an AI-native marketing team looks like.</li> <li>Prepare for and guide responses to sensitive or fast-moving issues in partnership with the appropriate teams.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>10+ years in social media, including at least 5 years leading social strategy for a global brand at the senior manager level or above, and accountable for the function's results.</li> <li>Experience owning a social function end to end, including strategy, budget, headcount, tooling, and results as the accountable leader. </li> <li>Experience leading teams, agencies, and cross-functional programs, with clear ownership of and accountability for outcomes.</li> <li>Depth in YouTube strategy, including owning and growing a brand or business channel, and can speak to programming decisions, video formats, packaging, and the metrics that actually move a channel.</li> <li>Hands-on experience growing LinkedIn and X as primary channels, with judgment about what content, format, and cadence work on each.</li> <li>Experience with paid social programs and how organic and paid social reinforce each other, including creative for paid, audience strategy, and interpreting paid performance data.</li> <li>Experience connecting social media programs to broader brand, communications, product, or
