title: Senior Software Engineer, Security Factory: Code Security
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Senior Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Security team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write and in the open source components they depend on.</p> <p>Your work spans complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the dependency analysis side, you teach the analysis engine what a project depends on. You parse dependency manifests, lockfiles, and SBOMs so the engine knows which libraries and frameworks are in play and how the code uses them. You also extend the service that turns security advisories into automated merge requests that update vulnerable dependencies. On the vulnerability detection side, you grow GitLab's security analysis engine with hybrid analyzers that blend rule-based detection and AI reasoning. You build and apply the tooling that develops, evaluates, and ships those analyzers, and you measure how well they find real problems. That work also expands coverage of the libraries, frameworks, and AI agent tooling that real-world applications are built on.</p> <p>These threads reinforce each other. What a project depends on, and how its code uses those dependencies, are parts of one picture, and this team works across all of it. We make thoughtful use of AI-assisted development tools in our daily work. We expect you to use them effectively and with good judgment.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for team initiatives from design through delivery, shipping with minimal guidance in partnership with the technical lead</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Design and ship analyzers that pair deterministic analysis capabilities with AI-driven analysis, and build the evaluation harnesses that measure their false positives and missed findings against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes detection rules mapped to CWE and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Package those analyzers for every place GitLab runs them, including CI jobs, AI agent workflows, and command-line tools, with findings reported in GitLab's standard security report formats</li> <li>Design and ship the manifest, lockfile, and SBOM parsing that tells the static analysis engine what a project depends on, and extend it to new ecosystems and formats</li> <li>Ship features across the automated remediation service that turns security advisories into dependency update merge requests, from sandboxed updates to merge request creation</li> <li>Solve technical problems of high scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, Engineering stakeholders such as Frontend and UX, and partner teams such as Code Scanning and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor Intermediate engineers through code review and pairing, and maintain our internal standards for style, maintainability, and best practices through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Substantial professional experience writing and testing production code in a systems language, particularly Go and/or Rust, with depth in at least one. We use both, plus Ruby on the remediation side and Python for some analyzers, and value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Familiarity with package managers and dependency management in one or more language ecosystems, such as npm, Maven, pip, Bundler, or Cargo. Experience building tooling around them is better still.</li> <li>Demonstrated application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE) and the software supply chain</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous problems and shipping with minimal guidance, with the self-motivation and organizational skills suited to a remote, largely asynchronous environment</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about technical problems, and to write design proposals that bring a team to a decision</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience evaluating AI-driven detection against labeled data, including measuring false positives and missed findings</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization at scale</li> <li>Hands-on program analysis experience, such as parsing, ASTs, or data-flow analysis</li> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Security team builds GitLab's code-level security scanning capabilities, spanning static application security testing and dependency scanning. We help developers find and fix security issues in both the code they write and the open source components they depend on, as early as possible.</p> <p>We work closely with the Static Analysis team on GitLab's SAST engines, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. AI-driven DevSecOps landscape.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Lead technical discovery, demonstrations, and validation to show how GitLab's AI-powered DevSecOps platform meets region's professional services arm, to promote consistent technical delivery and best practices across partner-led engagements.</li> <li>Represent GitLab at online and in-person marketing events, business leaders, guiding them through GitLab-supported transformation and helping them become GitLab advocates.</li> <li>Advise customers on modern software development, continuous integration and continuous deployment, security, and cloud practices, challenging existing approaches to improve return on investment.</li> <li>Serve as the voice of the customer across product management, engineering, sales, and marketing by sharing feedback, use cases, and competitive insights that inform the product roadmap and positioning.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience engaging with enterprise customers in technical presales, consulting, or similar roles and guiding them through solution design and evaluation.</li> <li>Proficiency across the software development lifecycle, including modern DevSecOps practices, continuous integration and continuous deployment workflows, and GitLab or comparable source control and collaboration platforms.</li> technical evaluations such as proofs of concept or proofs of value, contribute to tenders or audits, and design and run workshops or value stream assessments.</li> <li>Clear technical communication, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to adapt messages for practitioners and senior business and technical decision-makers and represent customer perspectives across transferable experience from related fields.</li> <li>Fluency in Korean and English.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>The Solutions Architect team is part of GitLab's Sales You'll dig into Linux systems, logs, and our Ruby on Rails codebase to troubleshoot performance issues, reproduce bugs, and contribute merge requests that fix problems at the source.</p> <p>You'll also improve our documentation, refine support processes in our issue tracker, and collaborate closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales so customer feedback directly shapes our roadmap. In your first year, you'll build deep expertise across a range of GitLab implementations, strengthen our ability to keep customers productive on both self-managed GitLab and GitLab.com software as a service, and help create tools and content that make support more efficient and effective for the entire team.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlab-detective">A tool to automatically check a GitLab Omnibus install for known issues</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos">A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting</a></li> <li><a href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/sosparser">A tool which turns log files into interactive tables to easily sort and filter columns</a></li> <li><a href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ci/chatops/">A ChatOps feature that makes it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</a></li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as an escalation point for difficult customer interactions and lead the resolution of complex issues through Zendesk tickets, merge requests, email, and video calls.</li> <li>Mentor and guide teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Advocate for and drive improvements to support practices, product quality, and reusable documentation and support content that directly influence team objectives.</li> <li>Collaborate with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales teams to shape product goals, roadmaps, and priorities while driving fixes and new features.</li> <li>Participate in regular weekday and weekend on-call rotations during daytime hours, providing emergency support for self-managed GitLab and software as a service customers and coordinating incident communications with the GitLab.com Production team.</li> <li>Participate in hiring by reviewing applications and assessments and joining interviews to help grow the Support team.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex, customer-facing technical cases from initial contact through triage, reproduction, bug reporting, resolution, and clear customer communication, including difficult or escalated interactions.</li> <li>Strong experience with Linux systems administration, scripting, Git, and continuous integration and continuous delivery in production or customer environments, with the ability to investigate issues at both the infrastructure and application levels.</li> <li>Ability to mentor teammates on complex troubleshooting and customer communication through pairing sessions, case reviews, and cross-team collaboration.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Product, Engineering, and Sales teams to turn customer feedback into product fixes, feature improvements, and roadmap priorities.</li> <li>Familiarity with DevOps practices and technologies such as Kubernetes and serverless computing, and an understanding of how different GitLab implementations operate and affect customers.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to learn, collaborate across teams, and apply transferable skills from related technical support or engineering roles.</li> <li>Fluent Korean language skills (required)</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>We're a globally distributed group of Support Engineers across the Americas, Europe, the Middle East, and Africa, and Asia-Pacific. You'll own the technical evaluation and validation stages of the sales cycle, guide customers through proofs of concept and value, and translate platform capabilities into outcomes that agency leaders, CIOs, CISOs, and procurement officers can defend in a budget request or an RFP evaluation.</p> <p>You'll partner closely with SLED account executives, channel partners, and systems integrators, provide technical guidance from first conversation through successful deployment, and bring the voice of the SLED customer back into Product, Sales, and Marketing.</p> <p><strong>Location and travel:</strong> The territory covers all states east of the Mississippi River. The candidate must reside in the Northeast part of the United States. This role requires up to 50% travel.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Engage SLED customers onsite and remotely, from state capitals to university campuses, with tailored demos, technical presentations, and hands-on workshops that tie GitLab to their mission.</li> <li>Partner with SLED account executives to shape account strategies that align with each customer's fiscal year budget cycle, legislative appropriations, IT modernization plans, and grant or federal pass through funding.</li> <li>Own the technical evaluation process, including proof of concept (POC) and proof of value (POV) design and delivery, and provide technical responses for RFIs, RFPs, RFQs, and security questionnaires.</li> <li>Support purchases made through cooperative purchasing agreements and statewide contract vehicles by working with channel and reseller partners.</li> <li>Guide customers through state and sector security requirements, such as GovRAMP and NIST frameworks, and show how GitLab's built in security, auditability, and deployment options reduce compliance burden.</li> <li>Help agencies and institutions modernize legacy and mainframe applications, such as unemployment insurance, tax, DMV, benefits, and student information systems, using GitLab and AI-assisted development to lower risk and offset shrinking pools of legacy skilled staff.</li> <li>Advise customers on adopting AI responsibly, including the GitLab Duo Agent Platform, in line with state AI policies, governance boards, and data privacy requirements.</li> <li>Lead the creation of Customer Success Plans that capture technical success criteria and handoff details, ensuring a smooth path to deployment and adoption, often for IT teams with limited capacity.</li> <li>Work alongside Account Executives to build data driven business cases that quantify delivery bottlenecks, giving customers a defensible basis for budget requests and clear evidence of return on taxpayer investment.</li> <li>Build relationships with CIOs, CISOs, agency directors, enterprise architects, faculty, research computing leaders, and procurement officers so they become advocates for GitLab, including across agencies and campuses that share services.</li> <li>Collaborate with systems integrators and state IT shared-services organizations to scale GitLab adoption across multiple agencies, local governments, or campuses.</li> <li>Serve as the SLED customer advocate internally, channeling feedback on procurement, compliance, and deployment needs to Product, Sales, and Marketing.</li> <li>Stay current on GitLab and related technologies, and create reusable SLED demos, reference architectures, and assets for customers and partners.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Background in technical pre-sales, consulting, or IT roles serving state agencies, local governments, or public, private, and research universities, where you guided customers through evaluations and solution design.</li> <li>Working knowledge of how SLED organizations buy technology: RFP and RFI cycles, cooperative purchasing agreements, statewide contracts, fiscal-year budgeting, and the role of resellers and systems integrators.</li> <li>Hands-on experience using GitLab and familiarity with modern software development and operations practices, such as CI/CD, DevSecOps, and automation.</li> <li>Experience with cloud, hybrid, and self-managed deployments in regulated environments, including government cloud regions, and an understanding of data residency and sovereignty concerns.</li> <li>Familiarity with security and compliance frameworks common in SLED, such as GovRAMP and NIST SP 800-53.</li> <li>Ability to connect technical solutions to mission outcomes, such as resident service delivery, cyber resilience, cost avoidance, and workforce efficiency, and to advise senior stakeholders on tradeoffs and options.</li> <li>Strong communication and relationship-building skills, including presenting to both technical teams and non-technical leaders such as agency heads, procurement officers, and university administrators.</li> <li>Openness to learning, seeking feedback, and building new skills, including familiarity with GitLab's Solutions Architect handbook and related resources.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have</strong></p> <ul> <li>Prior experience working in or for state or local government IT, or a university IT or research computing organization.</li> <li>Experience with legacy or mainframe modernization programs.</li> <li>Familiarity with AI governance practices in the public sector, such as AI use-case inventories, acceptable-use policies, and risk assessments.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> and adopt the GitLab DevSecOps platform. expertise in GitLab, DevSecOps, AI, and related cloud technologies, creating reusable examples, best practice guidance, and technical collateral for customers and partners.</li> <li value="8">Invest in your own growth and development through ongoing learning, mentorship, and knowledge sharing to continuously improve the impact of the Solutions Architect team.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Experience engaging with customers in technical pre-sales, consulting, or similar roles, guiding them through solution design and evaluation.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with the end-to-end software development lifecycle, including modern DevSecOps practices and continuous integration and continuous deployment workflows.</li> <li value="3">Hands-on experience with GitLab or comparable source control, continuous integration and continuous deployment, and collaboration platforms, and the ability to map platform capabilities to customer use cases.</li> <li value="4">Practical knowledge of cloud computing concepts and related technologies, with the ability to discuss deployment, security, and operations options with technical teams.</li> <li value="5">Ability to lead technical evaluations such as proofs of concept or proofs of value, contribute to tenders or audits, and design and run workshops or value stream assessments.</li> <li value="6">Clear technical communication and presentation skills, with the ability to adapt messages for practitioners through to senior business and technical decision makers.</li> <li value="7">Skill continuously develop professionally, including learning new technologies, deepening GitLab platform expertise, and applying transferable experience from related fields.</li> <li value="9">Fluency in Arabic.</li> </ul> <h2>About the team</h2> <p>The Solutions Architect team is part of GitLab's Sales organization and serves as the technical counterpart to Account Executives, with this role focused on opportunities across Southern EMEA and reporting into a regional Solutions Architect Manager. We work closely with Sales, Product Management, Engineering, and Marketing, collaborating asynchronously across regions to share best practices, create reusable technical collateral, and act as the voice of the customer. orchestrated to where a step should stay human-owned, and defend those calls once they're tested against real code.</li> <li>Discover and prioritize sources of friction across GitLab's SDLC, driving operates like a small, generalist group rather than one scoped to a single service.</li> <li>Apply distributed systems judgment to catch cases where generated code looks correct but breaks under concurrency, at scale, or across deployment topologies (including self-managed, dedicated, and multi-tenant environments), and coach others to do the same.</li> <li>Mentor senior and mid-level engineers on agent engineering practices and distributed systems judgment, through design reviews and pairing that raise the team's collective bar rather than just your own output.</li> <li>Collaborate with the India-based group a few times a week to align on the roadmap, and represent the team's technical progress to stakeholders in the Chief Technology Officer's organization.</li> <li>Serve as a bar raiser for the team's hiring, owning the Technical Leadership round for other Staff-level candidates as the team scales.</li> <li>Own a greenfield technical foundation from day one, with your scope and impact free to grow as the team scales.</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience building reliable agentic or large language model (LLM)-based systems, including multi-step orchestration, tool use, guardrails, and recovery.</li> <li>Ability to work autonomously in unfamiliar codebases and drive solutions from discovery through completion.</li> <li>Strong distributed systems and computer science fundamentals, including coordination, consistency, idempotency, rate limiting, failure modes, and degradation under load.</li> <li>Proficiency in Go, Rust, or Python, with the ability to read and modify code in the others.</li> <li>A track record of delivering results from unclear or incomplete requirements — able to take a complex, loosely specified problem and decompose it into a concrete proposal of small, shippable steps.</li> <li>Experience designing evaluation frameworks for systems where "looks plausible" and "is actually correct" are different questions, and a track record of raising the quality bar for a team's output, not just your own.</li> <li>A history of unblocking and enabling teammates — through design reviews, technical writing, or mentoring — and of engaging regularly with other teams to find where collaboration actually pays off.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Nonlinear Productivity — shortened internally to "NLP," with no relation to natural language processing — is one of GitLab's newest teams: a strategic incubation group that reports into AI Platform leadership under the direct sponsorship of the CTO. It's split into a US group (this role) and an India-based group working the same charter; the two sync on roadmap and tooling a few times a week but otherwise run day to day on their own. Solutions that prove out internally are the team's path to a monetized, customer-facing GitLab offering.</p> <p>It's a good fit for engineers who want technical ownership of something with no existing playbook, and a hand in defining a brand-new part of GitLab from its first commit.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. This range is intended to reflect the role's base salary rate in locations throughout the US. Grade level and salary ranges are determined through interviews and a review of education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities of the applicant, equity with other team members, alignment with market data, and geographic location. The base salary range does not include any bonuses, equity, or benefits. title: Staff Backend Engineer, Database Automation (Go)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2>An overview of this role</h2> <p>As a Senior or Staff Backend Engineer with the <a class="textLink" href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/engineering/data-engineering/database-excellence/">Database Excellence group</a>, you'll build and evolve database automation and PostgreSQL as a service capabilities for GitLab. The level will be determined during the hiring process. You'll use Go to automate the full lifecycle of PostgreSQL across GitLab's infrastructure, making database operations safer, more consistent, and easier to scale for databases that sit behind high-throughput, always-on internet services. You'll work closely with partner teams to shape how GitLab provisions and manages PostgreSQL in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-org/database-team/traffic-replay-poc">SQL Traffic Replay Tooling</a>, which validates upgrades and changes against real production workloads.</li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-org/database-team/backend/-/work_items/1">PostgreSQL as a Service Platform</a>, which provides standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management for internal product databases.</li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/groups/gitlab-com/gl-infra/data-access/dbo/-/work_items/75">PostgreSQL Major Version Upgrade Automation</a>, which supports safe, repeatable major upgrades at GitLab.com scale.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll do</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Design, build, and maintain Go-based automation that manages the full PostgreSQL lifecycle, including provisioning, configuration, upgrades, failover, scaling, and decommissioning, reducing reactive operational work that currently takes more than 80% of the team's time.</li> <li value="2">Build automation that works across infrastructure-as-code tooling and cloud infrastructure, and evaluate operator-based approaches as the platform evolves.</li> <li value="3">Use AI agents as a regular part of building and operating services, including implementation, review, and reducing repetitive work, while keeping the context agents need in the repository so the whole team can build on it.</li> <li value="4">Build for internet scale by designing automation and services for high-throughput, always-on production workloads, where GitLab.com traffic sets the bar for correctness, latency, and availability.</li> <li value="5">Integrate compute, storage, networking, identity and access management, and managed data services across cloud providers into one coherent PostgreSQL platform instead of creating bespoke setups for each database.</li> <li value="6">Build GitLab's PostgreSQL as a service platform to replace bespoke database setups with standardized, automated provisioning and lifecycle management, so supporting more databases doesn't require growing the operations team at the same rate.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate closely with product management, infrastructure, software delivery, and other engineering teams to design and ship high-performing solutions.</li> <li value="8">Research, design, and implement improvements to PostgreSQL performance, scalability, and data health, helping maintain more than 8 months of operational runway for all critical database saturation points.</li> <li value="9">Review database automation and Go changes from other engineers and contributors, with attention to safety, maintainability, and performance.</li> <li value="10">Document automation practices, PostgreSQL operational patterns, and guidance that helps engineers use and contribute to the platform.</li> <li value="11">Build safe, repeatable automation for PostgreSQL major version upgrades at GitLab.com scale, validating changes against real production traffic before rollout.</li> <li value="12">Operate what you build in production from end to end, using production feedback to guide each iteration.</li> <li value="12">Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it.</li> </ul> <h2>What you’ll bring</h2> <ul> <li value="1">Professional software engineering experience working with PostgreSQL in large, complex production environments, including experience building or operating a database-as-a-service product.</li> <li value="2">Proficiency with Go, including designing, implementing, testing, and reviewing backend services.</li> <li value="3">Experience developing Kubernetes operators, controllers, or similar automation for the lifecycle of stateful services, especially databases. You will work across endpoint management, identity, and security operations to improve how GitLab manages macOS, iOS, Windows, and Linux devices through Infrastructure-as-Code, Terraform, and GitOps workflows. automation for secure endpoint deployment, configuration, and lifecycle management using code-based workflows.</li> <li>Manage endpoint and SaaS security configuration through Terraform, version patching and software distribution approaches that align with security, compliance, and operational requirements.</li> <li>Partner with Information Technology, Security Operations, and Detection and Response teams to improve endpoint telemetry, detections, and response models.</li> <li>Drive process improvements that reduce manual work and lower risk by favoring automation, policy-driven controls, and auditable change management.</li> <li>Mentor engineers across Corporate Security and Information Technology, and serve as a senior escalation point for complex endpoint security issues.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>Experience designing and delivering endpoint, systems, or corporate security solutions in environments that require scalable, durable controls.</li> <li>Deep knowledge of endpoint management platforms such as Jamf Pro or FleetDM, especially for architecting and securing macOS environments.</li> <li>Strong hands-on ability with Terraform and Infrastructure-as-Code practices, including module design, state management, and pipeline-based deployment.</li> <li>Experience working with GitOps workflows where changes are managed through Git repositories, merge requests, code review, and automated pipelines.</li> <li> Strong proficiency in scripting or programming for automation and security tooling, such as bash, Python, PowerShell, or Go.</li> <li>Familiarity with cloud identity providers and directories, including platforms such as Okta, Google Workspace, LDAP.</li> <li>Ability to communicate clearly, collaborate across distributed teams, and work independently in an all-remote environment.</li> <li>Openness to bringing transferable experience from adjacent security, systems, or platform engineering backgrounds, along with a practical and security-focused approach to problem solving.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The Corporate Security Engineering team secures the internal environment GitLab team members use every day, including endpoints, identity systems, SaaS applications, and platforms that store sensitive internal data. of analytics and metrics platforms, graph data systems, CDC and warehouse integration.</li> <li>Hands-on experience building production AI-powered tool orchestration.</li> <li>Experience operating multi-tenant systems across SaaS and self-managed deployment.</li> <li>Direct communicator who builds alignment across teams.</li> <li>Bias to write things down and make reasoning legible.</li> </ul> customers consume GitLab data through Snowflake, Databricks, and BigQuery with no engineering dependencies.</li> <li>Publish GitLab observability as OpenTelemetry and broker the data-sharing title: Staff Product Manager, Agentic Test Intelligence
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As Staff Product Manager, Test & Code Coverage, you'll build product capabilities from initial discovery through launch and adoption. You'll help engineering teams understand why pipelines fail, improve test automation, and use code coverage to make better decisions about software quality and risk.</p> <p>You'll turn a technically complex problem space into a focused strategy, roadmap, and developer experience. Working closely with Engineering and Design, you'll explore how agents can diagnose failures, recommend next steps, and help teams recover safely. The goal isn't to add artificial intelligence (AI) for its own sake. It's to reduce manual work and help developers get back to a safe, shippable state without losing trust or control.</p> <p>At GitLab, our mission is simple: to enable everyone to contribute to and co-create the software that powers our world. You'll contribute to that mission by making testing and coverage insights more useful across the software development lifecycle.</p> <h2><strong>What you'll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Define and communicate the Test & Code Coverage product vision, strategy, and outcome-focused roadmap, from discovery through a minimum viable product, beta, launch, and continued iteration.</li> <li>Identify customer problems across pipeline failure diagnosis, test automation, test optimization, code coverage, and recovery. Build the case for investment, prioritize foundational and customer-facing work, and reshape or stop initiatives that aren't creating value.</li> <li>Work with Engineering to understand pipeline failures caused by flaky tests, testing gaps, environment issues, configuration problems, and coverage blind spots. Connect code changes, tests, pipeline behavior, historical patterns, and risk to help developers find a diagnosis and an actionable next step.</li> <li>Work directly with customers to understand how they author, maintain, select, prioritize, and debug tests. Connect test selection, test impact analysis, code coverage, and pipeline intelligence to reduce flaky tests, shorten feedback loops, and focus testing effort where it lowers the most risk.</li> <li>Partner with Engineering and Design to prototype agent-driven workflows for failure diagnosis, test authoring and repair, optimization, coverage analysis, and recovery. Make actions reviewable through evidence, confidence, human approval, and safe paths to propose code changes and merge requests. Use AI tools in your own product work to investigate problems, explore code and data, prototype concepts, and accelerate learning.</li> <li>Define and measure outcomes such as time to diagnose, time to recover, failure recurrence, test signal quality, and developer confidence. Validate problems and solutions with customers and learn from production usage.</li> <li>Partner across Product, Engineering, Design, Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing to connect testing insights with code review, pipelines, and release decisions. Turn customer evidence into clear narratives that support adoption and future investment.</li> <li>Lead through clear written communication, prioritization, and product judgment. Influence senior stakeholders, establish repeatable discovery and measurement practices, and mentor other product managers.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Experience owning complex technical products, platforms, or developer workflows at Staff, Senior Staff, Principal, or equivalent scope, including building a new product or capability from initial validation through launch and adoption.</li> <li>Strong product fundamentals in customer discovery, problem framing, prioritization, roadmap development, outcome measurement, and iterative delivery.</li> <li>Technical fluency in one or more relevant areas, such as software testing, test automation, code coverage, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), developer tools, DevOps, developer experience, quality engineering, or software delivery.</li> <li>An understanding of how engineering teams build, test, review, and ship software, and the ability to work with engineers on test architecture, pipeline behavior, code changes, data, integrations, reliability, and scale.</li> <li>Experience diagnosing technical problems and turning complex, noisy signals into clear user experiences and actionable workflows.</li> <li>Experience exploring AI or agent-driven solutions for developer workflows, with the judgment to distinguish useful automation from unsafe or low-confidence actions.</li> <li>Experience using customer conversations to understand problems and inform product decisions, communicating clearly in writing and conversation, and influencing across functions with shared ownership. You can work directly with developers, quality engineers, platform teams, engineering leaders, and executives, and move between strategy and implementation detail.</li> </ul> <h2><strong>About the team</strong></h2> <p>Our work brings together Product, Engineering, and Design, with input from Quality, Developer Experience, Customer Success, Support, and Product Marketing. title: Staff Product Manager,  RevOps & Finance Systems
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An Overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>We are seeking a Staff Product Manager to serve as an internal PM embedded within this team. This is not a traditional external-facing product role—it is an internal platform product leadership position. You will own the roadmap for our enterprise systems, act as the strategic voice of the business within engineering, and bring senior product craft to a team of Analysts and engineers who build and operate GitLab's revenue infrastructure. </p> <p>This role is ideal for a seasoned product leader who has deep Quote-to-Cash or Finance domain knowledge, thrives at the intersection of business strategy and technical execution, and is energized by mentoring high-performing teams through complex, multi-program environments.</p> <h3><strong>What You’ll Do  </strong></h3> <p><strong>Internal Product Roadmap Ownership</strong></p> <ul> <li>Define, own, and maintain the multi-quarter internal product roadmap for QTC and Finance Systems, covering Salesforce CPQ, Zuora Billing, Zuora Revenue, NetSuite, and the CDot metering platform.</li> <li>Translate business strategy from Finance, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Sales into sequenced, prioritized system capabilities with clear outcomes and success metrics.</li> <li>Balance competing program demands—stabilization, net-new capability delivery, and technical debt reduction—with transparent trade-off frameworks.</li> <li>Drive quarterly and annual planning ceremonies, partnering with Engineering Managers and Business Systems Analysts to align capacity with roadmap commitments.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Stakeholder Partnership & Requirements Translation</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary internal product voice for all QTC and Finance Systems initiatives, partnering closely with Finance, Accounting, Revenue Operations, Deal Desk, and Legal.</li> <li>Lead discovery, requirements workshops, and business process design sessions to translate complex financial and commercial requirements into actionable system specifications.</li> <li>Own the decision layer between "what the business needs" and "what engineering builds," resolving ambiguity with structured frameworks and documented decisions.</li> <li>Navigate cross-functional stakeholder dynamics including SOX compliance, audit controls, and revenue recognition governance (ASC 606/IFRS 15).</li> </ul> <p><strong>Team Mentorship & Capability criteria definition, and roadmap communication.</li> <li>Model and instill product management best practices—user story writing, prioritization frameworks (e.g., RICE, MoSCoW), sprint review discipline, and outcome tracking—across the team.</li> <li>Partner with leadership to evolve the operating model of the team from project-execution-focused to product-thinking-led, raising the bar for how ETA delivers business value.</li> <li>Provide structured feedback and growth coaching to BSAs on career development, helping analysts grow toward senior and lead levels.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Program Strategy & Delivery Oversight</strong></p> <ul> <li>Lead product strategy for major multi-quarter programs (e.g., consumption-based billing iterations, CLM/Order Forms, Zuora Product Catalog refactors, ERP optimization) from discovery through go-live.</li> <li>Define and maintain program-level dependency maps across concurrent workstreams, surfacing risks early and driving cross-team resolution.</li> <li>Own UAT strategy and acceptance criteria in collaboration with BSAs, ensuring system changes meet business requirements before production release.</li> <li>Support post-launch stabilization and continuous improvement cycles, prioritizing defect resolution and incremental enhancements based on business impact.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Systems Architecture Collaboration</strong></p> <ul> <li>Partner with Enterprise Architects and Engineering Managers to evaluate build-vs-buy-vs-configure decisions for new capabilities.</li> <li>Bring informed opinions on QTC platform architecture trade-offs (e.g., billing model design, middleware integration patterns, revenue recognition rule configuration) based on deep domain knowledge.</li> <li>Stay current on platform roadmaps for Salesforce, Zuora, and NetSuite, identifying opportunities to leverage native capabilities before custom builds.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></h3> <ul> <li>8+ years of product management experience, with at least 3 years in an internal platform PM, enterprise applications PM, or systems product leadership role.</li> <li>Deep domain expertise in Quote-to-Cash systems: Salesforce CPQ, Zuora Billing, Zuora Revenue, and NetSuite ERP are the core stack—hands-on configuration or implementation experience strongly preferred.</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to own and communicate multi-quarter internal product roadmaps to senior business and technology stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong command of revenue lifecycle processes: opportunity-to-quote, order management, billing and collections, revenue recognition (ASC 606), and financial close.</li> <li>Experience operating in a SOX-controlled environment with an understanding of audit trails, approval workflows, and change management requirements for financial systems.</li> <li>Track record of successfully running complex, multi-program delivery environments with competing priorities and shared engineering resources.</li> <li>Sufficient technical fluency to engage meaningfully with engineering on API design, data model decisions, and integration trade-offs—without needing to write code.</li> <li>Experience with consumption-based or usage-based billing models</li> </ul> <p> </p> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>You'll be joining the Revenue Lifecycle & Finance Systems team within GitLab's Enterprise Technology Architecture organization. Our team is responsible for the systems and processes that power GitLab's entire revenue lifecycle—from configure-price-quote through contract execution, billing, revenue recognition, and financial close. </p> <p>We are in an exciting and demanding phase: transitioning GitLab's go-to-market from a pure subscription model toward consumption-based offerings while simultaneously modernizing our core platforms. This role will be central to shaping how that evolution happens—and how the team grows in capability and product maturity alongside it.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>An overview of this role</strong></span></h2> <p>As a Staff Product Manager on the Tenant Scale area within Infrastructure Platforms, you’ll set product direction for how GitLab supports large, complex customers as they grow across departments, projects, and regions. This role focuses on the product choices needed to make tenant data more portable, scalable, and ready for a unified deployment model across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and, over time, Self-Managed. You’ll work on problems that sit at the intersection of product strategy, infrastructure, and customer needs, including how we build a platform to horizontally scale our SaaS architecture, how to enable tenant movement between environments, how isolation and regional requirements are handled, and what needs to be in place to support a more cellular architecture.</p> <p>At the Staff level, your scope extends beyond a single group. Your direction will inform the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction, you’ll make the investment case for unified deployment capabilities, and you’ll be a recognized authority, inside and outside GitLab, on multi-tenant and cellular SaaS architecture. In your first year, you’ll partner closely with engineering and product peers to define requirements, drive alignment, and move this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on, while coaching fellow product managers as they pick up work from the shared pool.</p> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What you’ll do</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Drive</strong> product strategy and direction for tenant scale and unified deployment capabilities across GitLab.com, Dedicated, and future deployment models, informing the broader Infrastructure Platforms direction and moving this work from concept into a deployment model teams can build on in your first year.</li> <li><strong>Set</strong> quarterly and annual plans for tenant portability and platform unification, breaking large epics into issues and minimal valuable changes (MVCs) and practicing iteration across multiple groups.</li> <li><strong>Define</strong> requirements for our unified deployment platform, including the capabilities needed before tenants can be hosted in a unified deployment unit.</li> <li><strong>Partner</strong> closely with engineering counterparts and highly technical teams to turn infrastructure constraints and platform needs into clear product direction.</li> <li><strong>Collaborate</strong> with product peers across the platforms organization, including teams working on GitLab.com and adjacent infrastructure areas, and manage with influence to align work that spans more than one group.</li> <li><strong>Engage</strong> with internal and external customers to understand needs related to isolation, regional deployment, compliance, and operational readiness, using qualitative interviews to find patterns and sharpen problem statements.</li> <li><strong>Build</strong> business cases for investment in tenant scale and unified deployment, including build, buy, and partner options, the cost of isolation, regionality, and compliance, and the expected benefits.</li> <li><strong>Facilitate</strong> tradeoff discussions around scalability, tenant encapsulation, deployment consistency, and platform unification, and escalate cleanly to the right level of leadership when decisions or progress are blocked.</li> <li><strong>Translate</strong> complex technical concepts into product plans, priorities, and documentation that align distributed teams on delivery milestones for tenant portability and platform unification, using error budgets and other performance indicators to inform direction.</li> <li><strong>Represent</strong> GitLab as a trusted voice on cellular architecture and tenant scale in customer calls, events, and other external forums.</li> <li><strong>Coach</strong> fellow product managers on direction updates, customer validation, and GitLab’s architecture and tech stack, and support a collaborative team model where product managers share ownership across a common pool of work and step into the areas where they can have the most impact.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></span></h2> <ul> <li><strong>Experience</strong> managing product work in technical domains such as infrastructure, scalability, platform architecture, software delivery, or cloud services, with results delivered across a range of product areas rather than a single one.</li> <li><strong>Ability</strong> to work effectively with deeply technical engineering teams and build credibility in discussions about system design, deployment models, and platform constraints.</li> <li><strong>Knowledge</strong> of how SaaS or platform-based systems scale, including concepts such as multitenancy, horizontal scalability, autoscaling, workload isolation, and production readiness, and the ability to build a deep understanding of GitLab’s architecture and tech stack and coach others on it.</li> <li><strong>Comfort</strong> working with customers or internal stakeholders on complex requirements, including operational, compliance, or regional deployment needs.</li> <li><strong>Skill</strong> in turning ambiguous technical problems into clear product strategy, quarterly and annual plans, priorities, and actionable work.</li> <li><strong>Expertise</strong> in qualitative customer interviewing and product validation, with the ability to teach those techniques to others.</li> <li><strong>Experience</strong> building business cases, including weighing build, buy, and partner options and forecasting benefits against the competitive landscape.</li> <li><strong>Experience</strong> collaborating across product, engineering, user experience, and other cross-functional partners in a distributed environment, using iteration and influence to raise the performance of peers beyond your own group.</li> <li><strong>Strength</strong> in clear written and verbal communication, especially when explaining complex infrastructure topics to different audiences, with excellent presentation skills at every level of the company.</li> <li><strong>Recognition</strong> as a thought leader in a relevant domain, internally and externally, for example through speaking, writing, or representing your company at customer events and conferences.</li> <li><strong>Openness</strong> to candidates who bring transferable experience from engineering, technical support, or adjacent product roles relevant to large-scale platforms.</li> </ul> <h2><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><strong>About the team</strong></span></h2> <p>The team sits within Infrastructure Platforms and works on foundational platform capabilities. It partners closely with engineering, adjacent product managers, and internal customers across regions, with a strong emphasis on GitLab’s asynchronous working style and long-term platform thinking. Product managers on the team share ownership of a common pool of work; at the Staff level, you’ll help guide how that work is prioritized and mentor teammates as they take it on.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Your daily work will span architectural design reviews, technical prototyping, and establishing scalable patterns that enable engineering teams to execute autonomously.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Partner with engineering and product leadership across GitLab, developing enough context in their domains to anticipate security problems rather than react to them</li> <li>Lead security architecture and design work for strategic initiatives, and provide direction to the cross-functional teams delivering them</li> <li>Identify, assess, and prioritise systemic security risks, and act as Security Owner for high-priority items in the Product Security Risk Register, co-executing remediation with the teams who own the code</li> <li>Codify recurring security decisions into reusable artifacts — guardrails, standards, design patterns,skills, and reference threat models — delivered into developer and AI coding tool workflows</li> <li>Build proofs of concept and prototypes to unblock engineering teams and shorten the distance between a security requirement and a working implementation</li> <li>Conduct security architecture reviews for large or strategic projects, and coordinate with Application Security so that review coverage is comprehensive and correctly prioritised</li> <li>Threat model new and existing systems, and establish the patterns that let teams threat model their own work</li> <li>Work with Security Research on proactive exploration of unknown risks in GitLab's architecture</li> <li>Anticipate emerging security challenges and propose architectural responses before they reach implementation</li> <li>Mentor security engineers across the division, and represent security architecture to engineering audiences</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Depth in application security architecture, including authentication and authorization models, privilege escalation, multi-tenant isolation, and trust boundary analysis</li> <li>Experience securing distributed systems, including service-to-service authentication, secrets handling, and the failure modes of security decisions made across process boundaries</li> <li>Working knowledge of software supply chain security: build and release integrity, artifact provenance, and dependency risk</li> <li>A track record of proactive architecture work — identifying risk before it becomes an incident, and designing something that prevents a class of problem rather than an instance of one</li> <li>Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships with engineering leadership and influence technical direction through expertise rather than gatekeeping</li> <li>Experience defining security standards or patterns that teams adopted without being compelled to</li> <li>The ability to operate strategically while remaining hands-on, including reading unfamiliar code, building prototypes, and contributing changes</li> <li>Clear written communication, and the ability to make a security argument to an engineering audience that does not already agree with it</li> <li>A view on how security guidance should be authored and delivered for You'll turn executive intent into workstreams, coordinate senior stakeholders across Sales, Customer Experience, Product, Marketing, Renewals, Professional Services, Data, and Enablement, and make the tactical calls that keep the portfolio honest.</p> <p>This is a founding seat reporting to the CCO while the broader Programs function is built, and the reporting line may evolve as the team scales. In your first year, every CCO-level program will have a clear owner other than the CCO, leadership will trust your data-grounded view of program health, and the portfolio will deliver measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>What you'll do</p> <ul> <li>Own execution and business outcomes across CCO-level programs, including go-to-market transformation, renewal and retention motions, product feedback loops, and executive sponsorship for top accounts.</li> <li>Turn CCO direction into workstreams with clear owners, dependencies, and timelines.</li> <li>Coordinate senior stakeholders across Sales, Customer Experience, Product, Marketing, Renewals, Professional Services, Data, and Enablement, holding them accountable without direct authority.</li> <li>Surface stalled work, unowned risks, and slipping timelines so the CCO has a reliable, real-time view of the portfolio.</li> <li>Recommend scope changes, re-sequencing, or ending a program when it is not delivering value.</li> <li>Drive follow-through from executive meetings by tracking decisions and action items to completion.</li> <li>Track program health using data, connect execution to retention, expansion, adoption, and ARR outcomes, and communicate executive-ready narratives.</li> <li>Build shared standards for tracking, reporting, and handoffs, and iterate plans with functional leaders based on field feedback.</li> </ul> <p>What you'll bring</p> <ul> <li>Experience leading complex, cross-functional strategic programs at the executive level and turning ambiguous direction into delivered outcomes without a fully scoped brief.</li> <li>Experience in Customer Experience, go-to-market, or revenue-facing functions such as Customer Success, Renewals, Sales, or Revenue Operations, with fluency in retention, expansion, and adoption motions and how they contribute to ARR.</li> <li>The ability to influence senior stakeholders, including executives, and hold them accountable to commitments without formal authority.</li> <li>Judgment to make high-stakes tactical recommendations under ambiguity, including when data supports changing direction or ending a program.</li> <li>Data fluency to assess program health, diagnose where work is breaking down, and recommend a data-informed next step.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, with the ability to move between an executive-ready narrative and execution-level detail.</li> <li>Comfort operating without established infrastructure and helping build the function's operating model.</li> <li>Reliable follow-through and the ability to navigate conflict and competing priorities across a broad stakeholder group.</li> </ul> <p>About the team</p> <p>You'll be the first Program Manager supporting CX Executive initiatives and the founding hire in a Programs function that will grow as the CCO's highest-priority cross-functional initiatives outgrow ad hoc ownership. The team works across the customer lifecycle, from go-to-market strategy and product feedback through renewal, expansion, and executive relationships with large accounts. title: Staff Regional Marketing Manager, West
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Staff Regional Marketing Manager, you will own regional marketing for the sales team in your territory and set the standard for how the regional team plans and runs its work. You will choose, plan, and run the events and campaigns that create, expand, and accelerate pipeline in your region, and you will move easily between high-level strategy and creative, detailed execution. Staff is a leadership-level individual contributor role: you lead through the work you build and ship, not through direct reports. In a modern marketing organization, that means building and running your own plans, programs, measurement, and AI-assisted automation instead of handing them off, and it suits builders who are comfortable being a leader without a team to manage. Your audience is CIOs, CTOs, VPs of engineering and platform, and the security leaders who govern how their teams ship software. You will judge audience quality by seniority and buying role, not headcount, so you will need to understand how they work and what they want from a vendor.</p> <p>You will support both direct and channel sales teams, work with GitLab partners on Channel and Alliance Marketing activities, and partner with external agencies and third parties to prepare and run campaigns. As a senior individual contributor, you will mentor other regional marketers, help build and improve team process, and share best practices with regional peers by planning and operating transparently. Your impact is measured in pipeline: the target is 10X spend contribution to sales pipeline for your region, with your regional budget spent within 5% variance. This role supports one of our sales regions (AMER, EMEA, or APAC), and involves travel up to 50% of the time.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li>Drive results for your region as its marketing leader: own the pipeline and growth outcomes, and go beyond events and experiences to bring partners in to drive marketing across channels, in support of growth through our revenue team.</li> <li>Adapt digital and content marketing programs to the needs of your regional sales team.</li> <li>Create, expand, and accelerate sales opportunities through regional and account-focused campaigns that promote GitLab’s products and services, within the marketing strategy.</li> <li>Set regional event and campaign strategy, with discretion over which events and campaigns best support regional sales goals, and manage events onsite, including logistics, booth staffing, and swag.</li> <li>Project manage every campaign from start to finish, following the GitLab process, so each one meets its objectives, arrives on time, and stays within budget, then measure and report on its effectiveness.</li> <li>Lead cross-functional work to drive demand generation and regional marketing plans, and advocate for your sales region within marketing and for marketing with your sales team.</li> <li>Support Channel and Alliance Marketing activities with GitLab partners, from campaign approval through execution.</li> <li>Work with external agencies and third parties to prepare, manage, and execute campaigns.</li> <li>Mentor and guide regional marketing specialists and managers, and lead in building and driving process within the team.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li>Proven ability to build and execute  a regional strategy, with a record of delivering, accelerating, and expanding sales pipeline through regional marketing.</li> <li>Experience supporting both direct sales and channel sales teams, and in enterprise solution demand creation and regional marketing.</li> <li>Exemplary analytical skills and a proven aptitude for using data to optimize program performance and inform future strategies.</li> <li>Excellent communication skills, with a proven ability to convey ideas and data clearly in writing and in presentations to a variety of audiences, without a fear of over-communicating. title: Staff Security Governance Engineer, Policies & Standards
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h4><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h4> <p>As a Staff Security Governance Engineer, you will be the individual contributor who owns how GitLab writes, maintains, communicates, and measures its security policies and standards. You will turn emerging regulations, including AI regulation, into clear requirements that engineering, product, and legal teams can act on, and you will use automation to keep governance lightweight and continuous rather than a point-in-time exercise. You will sit on the Security Governance team within Security Assurance and work closely with Security Compliance, Security Risk, and GRC Engineering. You will report to the Director, Customer Trust & Security Governance.</p> <h4><strong>What you'll do</strong></h4> <ul> <li><em>Policies and standards</em></li> <ul> <li>Own the end-to-end lifecycle of GitLab's security policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines: drafting, stakeholder review, approval, publication, annual review, and retirement.</li> <li>Define and run the exception management process, including risk-based approvals, expiry tracking, and trend reporting that shows where policies need to change.</li> <li>Run policy attestation and investigate non-adherence.</li> <li>Keep policies clear, practical, and aligned with how GitLab's engineering teams work in a DevSecOps environment.</li> </ul> <li><em>Regulatory and framework alignment</em></li> <ul> <li>Monitor emerging regulations and standards (e.g., EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001, sector or regional requirements) and partner with Legal well ahead of compliance deadlines to assess impact and update policy.</li> <li>Maintain mappings between our policies and frameworks such as SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, so requirements are written once and reused.</li> </ul> <li><em>Measurement and assurance</em></li> <ul> <li>Define KPIs for policy adherence and report trends to Security leadership.</li> <li>Run targeted internal assessments of adherence and drive remediation to closure.</li> <li>Support audit activities by coordinating evidence, testing, and remediation management.</li> </ul> <li><em>Customer trust</em></li> <ul> <li>Support customer questionnaires and customer meetings, and help turn recurring customer requests into better policies and self-service content.</li> </ul> <li><em>Automation and AI</em></li> <ul> <li>Identify and implement automation and AI-assisted workflows for policy management, evidence collection, control monitoring, and assessment work, in partnership with GRC Engineering.</li> </ul> <li><em>Technical leadership</em></li> <ul> <li>Act as a technical and program leader across Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering, influencing without direct authority.</li> <li>Mentor other team members and help set the direction of the Security Governance roadmap.</li> </ul> </ul> <h4><strong>What you'll bring</strong></h4> <ul> <li>10+ years in security governance, GRC, or IT risk, with hands-on ownership of a policy and standards lifecycle and measurable outcomes, ideally at a global technology company.</li> <li>Working knowledge of SOC 2, ISO 27001, ISO 42001, FedRAMP, and NIST CSF, including how to put them into practice, not only how to read them</li> <li>Experience creating and maintaining an enterprise Information Security Management System (ISMS), ideally including hands on involvement in ISO 27001 certification or recertification.<span class="screenreader-hidden-offscreen"> </span></li> <li>Understanding of cloud, SaaS, and DevSecOps practices, and the ability to write policy that engineers will follow.</li> <li>A risk-based mindset that balances compliance with real security risk.</li> <li>Demonstrated use of automation or AI to reduce manual GRC work.</li> <li>Strong written and verbal communication, including translating technical concepts for engineers, executives, auditors, and customers.</li> <li>Experience collaborating with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering.</li> <li>Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CISA, or similar are highly desirable.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>What success looks like</strong></h4> <ul> <li>First 30 days: Assessed the current policy library and exception process, built relationships with key stakeholders, and proposed a prioritized roadmap.</li> <li>First 90 days: Uplift the existing security policy library to align with NIST CSF, ISO 27001/27017/27018/42001, and PCI-DSS.</li> <li>First 120 days: A refreshed review cadence is in place, exception reporting is running, and can demonstrate a measurable improvement in policy adherence.</li> <li>First six months: Develop Policy as Code and collaborate with Security, Product, Legal, and Engineering for implementation into existing workflows.</li> </ul> <h4><strong>About the team</strong></h4> <p>The Security Assurance organization helps GitLab build and maintain trust by strengthening how we approach security, compliance, and risk. Security Governance sits within it and owns customer trust, security awareness, policies and standards, and other governance functions. Our counterparts are Security Compliance, Security Risk, and GRC Engineering. <br><br>You will join a small team of four direct reports under the Director, where each person has broad scope and visible impact. We work remote-first and asynchronously, and we write things down and share them openly, so you'll draft and revise policies and standards in the open with input from Security, Legal, Product, and Engineering.</p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact.
