Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h3> <p>As a Staff Backend Engineer on GitLab's Security Factory: Code Scanning team, you help developers find and fix security issues. Those issues live in the code they write, and you set the technical direction for the static analysis engine that finds them.</p> <p>Your work spans two complementary parts of a complete security analysis. On the engine side, you shape how the static analysis toolkit models a program: parsing source into intermediate representations, resolving symbols, building call graphs, and tracking tainted data across files and languages. You define the architecture and specifications the team builds against, and you delegate component specifications within them to engineers and to the AI agents that implement them. On the evaluation side, you build and apply tooling that tests, measures, and validates what the engine finds against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities.</p> <p>What the engine can model and how we measure what it finds are parts of one picture. As a Staff engineer you hold that picture, shape the long-range technical goals of the team, and raise the bar for every engineer on it. We build the engine with AI agents that write and review code from written specifications, under human direction. We expect you to direct that work effectively and with good judgment, and to help the team do the same.</p> <h3><strong>What you do</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Act as the directly responsible individual (DRI) for the team's highest-scope initiatives from design through delivery, shipping large features with minimal guidance and shaping the long-range goals of the team</li> <li>Bring systems built by one engineer to team ownership through documentation, tests, and shared review</li> <li>Set the technical direction for the AI-assisted tooling that implements, reviews, and validates engine changes and findings, design the checks that decide whether an agent-written change or generated result is fit to merge, and measure detection quality against benchmark applications with known vulnerabilities, raising the bar for what counts as a trustworthy result. That includes static application security testing (SAST) rules mapped to CWE and OWASP, and the test fixtures that prove they work.</li> <li>Own the architecture of the program model (parsing, symbol resolution, intermediate representations, call graphs, and taint and data-flow analysis) and of the pipeline that turns source code into findings, and define how both extend to new languages and frameworks</li> <li>Solve technical problems of the highest scope and complexity, actively seek out difficult impediments affecting the whole team, and advocate for improvements to quality, security, and performance with Product Management, UX, and partner teams such as Code Security and Composition Analysis</li> <li>Mentor all engineers on the team through code review and pairing, remove blockers to their autonomy, and shepherd the definition and improvement of our internal standards through review</li> <li>Participate in on-call rotations to assist troubleshooting product operations, security operations, and urgent engineering issues</li> <li>Define the overarching architecture and specification documents for the engine, delegate component specifications within them, and drive their implementation by AI agents and engineers working independently through phased plans, small reviewable units of change, and specifications kept in lockstep with the code</li> <li>Build and maintain the harness, agent instructions, and agentic skills that keep agent-written code trustworthy, including separate coding and reviewing agents, rules and tests the coding agents cannot change, independent review panels of agents from different model providers, and performance, API, and dependency gates, with risky changes escalated to human review</li> <li>Stay current with research in program analysis and security, run AI-assisted research and spikes, and turn the findings into prototypes, proposals, and upstream contributions, including responsible disclosure of findings in open source projects</li> <li>Take part in on-call or operational support where your team’s ownership model requires it</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What you bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Experience building your own LLM tooling, such as a harness, an agent pipeline, or evaluations, with the judgment to know when output is trustworthy and when it isn't</li> <li>Extensive professional experience writing, testing, and reviewing production code in Rust, Go, or a comparable systems language, with depth in at least one. The engine is Rust, the analyzer wrapper is Go, and the monolith integration is Ruby, and we value willingness to work across them.</li> <li>Experience with performance optimization and with containerized workflows and CI/CD (we use Docker heavily)</li> <li>A deep program analysis and static analysis background, such as parsing and ASTs, intermediate representations (SSA, control-flow and call graphs), taint and data-flow analysis, type inference, incremental and fixpoint computation, or writing detection rules, with the ability to read, evaluate, and apply the research literature</li> <li>Deep application security experience, such as vulnerability research, secure code review, or writing detection rules, and fluency with vulnerability classes (OWASP Top 10, CWE)</li> <li>Demonstrated capacity to communicate clearly and concisely about complex technical, architectural, and organizational problems, and to write architecture and design specifications that bring a team to a decision</li> <li>A track record of taking ownership of ambiguous, team-wide problems and shipping them from concept to production with minimal guidance, with specific, regular async updates on progress, blockers, risks, and next steps</li> <li>Experience defining a system's overarching architecture, delegating component specifications to engineers and AI agents, and getting them implemented reliably</li> <li>A track record of mentoring engineers, raising a team's technical bar, and influencing technical direction by achieving consensus with peers and leadership</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Helpful experience</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Familiarity with popular web or mobile application frameworks and how they handle input, data, and configuration</li> <li>Experience designing guardrails for agent-written code, such as mutation testing, fuzzing, and CI gates the coding agent cannot modify</li> <li>A record of engaging with the research community, such as publications, tool papers, or upstream open source contributions in program analysis or security</li> </ul> <h3><strong>About the team</strong></h3> <p>The Security Factory: Code Scanning team develops GitLab's SAST capabilities for customer software repositories.</p> <p>We work closely with the Code Security team on scanning rules & flows, with Composition Analysis on the broader software supply chain, and with other groups across the Sec Section. We rely heavily on asynchronous work across time zones.</p> <div class="c-message_actions__container c-message__actions"> </div> <div><span style="font-size: xx-small;"><span style="color: white;">Remote-Global</span></span></div><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h2><strong>An overview of this role</strong></h2> <p>As a Subject Matter Expert (SME), you'll be the deepest technical voice in the field for one product group, helping customers make technical decisions on GitLab's most important opportunities, roughly the top 10% by size or complexity.</p> <p>Account Solutions Architects (Account SAs) will bring you into prioritized opportunities. The Account SA owns the opportunity; you own your product group's success within it. You'll work directly with Product and Engineering, bringing customer needs and field insights into roadmap discussions. You'll also help the wider Solutions Architecture team build expertise through reusable assets, enablement, and coaching.</p> <p>You'll specialize in one product group, not all four. In Security & Compliance, you'll focus on GitLab Ultimate, application security, Dependency Firewall, software supply chain security, compliance, and artificial intelligence (AI) governance. In Platform, you'll focus on GitLab Dedicated, self-managed deployments, bring your own model, and cloud and hybrid architecture. In Core DevSecOps, you'll focus on GitLab Premium, continuous integration and continuous delivery (CI/CD), source code management, Orbit, Artifact Central, and migrations. DevSecOps brings development, security, and operations together across software delivery. In AI & Competitive, you'll focus on GitLab Duo Agent Platform, agentic workflows, AI-native development, competitive displacement including GitHub, and migrations.</p> <p>Your success will be measured by technical win rate and bookings on SME-engaged opportunities, product-category commit attainment and consumption growth in your region, and Proof of Value (PoV) conversion rate, evaluation cycle time, and time from technical win to production use. We'll also measure how often Account SAs reuse your assets, their confidence in handling your product group without escalation, and the quality and impact of your feedback to Product.</p> <h2><strong>What you’ll do</strong></h2> <ul> <li>Act as the technical authority for your product group on prioritized opportunities, from discovery and architecture through trials and PoV evaluations.</li> <li>Lead technical deep dives, workshops, and executive briefings that connect product capabilities to business outcomes and explain how GitLab differs from competing solutions.</li> <li>Design and improve standardized PoV templates with clear, repeatable success criteria. Account SAs own the customer PoV; you'll contribute product-specific content and expertise while keeping the evaluation connected to the broader GitLab platform.</li> <li>Equip account teams for product launches with Product Management and Product Marketing. title: Strategic Account Executive - Brazil
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><p><strong>An overview of this role</strong></p> <p>As an <strong>Strategic Account Executive</strong>, you’ll help expand GitLab’s presence across Brazil by building trusted relationships with senior leaders at large organizations and guiding them through complex platform decisions. You’ll use a consultative sales approach to connect customer business needs with our AI-powered DevSecOps platform, helping teams improve developer productivity, reduce security and compliance risk, and move software delivery forward with more confidence. In this role, you’ll support strategic accounts across the full customer journey, from early conversations through adoption, while helping us position GitLab as a leading DevSecOps partner in the Brazilian market.</p> <p>You’ll work across pre-sales, post-sales, partner, marketing, and support teams, and we’ll rely on you to bring strong account leadership, customer outcomes, and clear communication in <strong>English and Portuguese</strong>. Over your first year, your impact will come from building account plans for large organizations, developing new opportunities, and helping customers successfully adopt GitLab in ways that align to their business goals.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>Lead strategic account activity for large prospects and customers across Brazil, providing direction throughout pre-sales and post-sales engagements.</p> </li> <li> <p>Develop opportunities within enterprise accounts through prospecting, relationship building, and a consultative understanding of customer business needs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Create account plans and customer proposals that clearly connect GitLab capabilities to organizational priorities and transformation goals.</p> </li> <li> <p>Coordinate with pre-sales, post-sales, and support teams to support successful product rollout and customer adoption.</p> </li> <li> <p>Generate qualified pipeline in partnership with strategic channel partners and support new customer development efforts.</p> </li> <li> <p>Contribute customer feedback and product ideas to GitLab’s public issue tracker to represent the voice of the customer.</p> </li> <li> <p>Prepare activity and forecast reports, and help analyze wins and losses to improve future sales execution.</p> </li> <li> <p>Collaborate with marketing, account teams, product managers, and technical teams to share lessons learned and communicate customer needs clearly.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll bring</strong></p> <ul> <li> <p>5+ years experience selling into large organizations and navigating complex enterprise sales cycles with multiple stakeholders.</p> </li> <li> <p>Ability to build and manage executive-level customer relationships with a high degree of ownership and follow-through.</p> </li> <li> <p>Skill in consultative selling, including shaping proposals, presentations, and formal quotes around customer business needs.</p> </li> <li> <p>Strength in negotiation, presentation, and closing conversations in a clear and effective way.</p> </li> <li> <p>Comfort working independently on complex projects while coordinating with cross-functional teams.</p> </li> <li> <p>Fluency in English and Portuguese for customer-facing and internal communication.</p> </li> <li> <p>Familiarity with GitLab or related tools, including Git, software development tools, application lifecycle management, or security and application security tools.</p> </li> <li> <p>Alignment with GitLab’s values, with openness to transferable experience from adjacent technical or enterprise software environments.</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The team focuses on growing GitLab’s enterprise business by helping large organizations adopt a single platform for software delivery, security, and collaboration. This role works closely with cross-functional partners across sales, solutions, support, marketing, and product, and contributes to an asynchronous, distributed way of working that values transparency, accountability, and shared customer insight. All of our roles are remote, however some roles may carry specific location-based eligibility requirements. Our Talent Acquisition team can help answer any questions about location after starting the recruiting process.  </p> <p><strong>Privacy Policy: </strong>Please review our <a href="https://handbook.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/candidate-faq/recruitment-privacy-policy/" target="_blank">Recruitment Privacy Policy.</a> Your privacy is important to us.</p> <p>GitLab is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. GitLab’s policies and practices relating to recruitment, employment, career development and advancement, promotion, and retirement are based solely on merit, regardless of race, color, religion, ancestry, sex (including pregnancy, lactation, sexual orientation, gender identity, or gender expression), national origin, age, citizenship, marital status, mental or physical disability, genetic information (including family medical history), discharge status from the military, protected veteran status (which includes disabled veterans, recently separated veterans, active duty wartime or campaign badge veterans, and Armed Forces service medal veterans), or any other basis protected by law. GitLab will not tolerate discrimination or harassment based on any of these characteristics. If you have a disability or special need that requires <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/people-policies/inc-usa/#reasonable-accommodation" target="_blank">accommodation</a>, please let us know during the <a href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/hiring/interviewing/#adjustments-to-our-interview-process" target="_blank">recruiting process</a>.</p></div>

title: Strategic Partnerships Director
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.</p> <p>The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. <a href="https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OuZIb5zszQI">Co-create the future with us</a> as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.</p> <p>*<em>Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.</em></p></div><h3>An overview of this role</h3> <p>As the Director, Strategic Partnerships, you will own GitLab's relationships with its two major cloud infrastructure partners: AWS and Google Cloud. This is a single-threaded owner role, reporting to the VP, Corporate Development & Strategic Partnerships. You will shape partnership strategy from the top down and drive execution from the ground up, this is as much about running the weekly grind of a partnership as it is about setting its direction, turning strategic relationships into durable business outcomes.</p> <p>You will own the commercial relationship end-to-end: managing GitLab's cloud infrastructure spend and consumption commitments, and leading renewal negotiations for enterprise agreements (e.g., EDPs, MACCs, or equivalent) before they come due. You will also own the technical and go-to-market side of each relationship: driving product integrations, shaping joint go-to-market strategy, and connecting GitLab's product roadmap and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives. This is not a co-sell, channel, or revenue-through-partners role. Success here looks like disciplined commercial ownership, technical integration depth, and renewal outcomes that protect and grow GitLab's position, not partner-sourced pipeline or quota attainment.</p> <p>This role sits close to GitLab's evolving AI strategy and the future of our AI-powered DevSecOps platform. You will develop a clear point of view, represent these partnerships with senior stakeholders, and personally drive the day-to-day work that spans multi-year planning and weekly execution, chasing down blockers, keeping workstreams on track, and doing the detailed follow-through yourself rather than delegating it.</p> <h3>What you'll do</h3> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary owner and point of contact for GitLab's cloud infrastructure partnerships with AWS and Google Cloud, personally accountable for the direction, operating rhythm, and outcomes of each.</li> <li>Own the full commercial lifecycle of each relationship: negotiating rates and terms, tracking consumption against committed spend, and leading renewal negotiations well ahead of contract expiration.</li> <li>Manage cloud infrastructure spend as a standing responsibility, partnering with Finance/FinOps on forecasting, true-ups, and cost optimization across both hyperscalers.</li> <li>Drive product integrations with each partner, working directly with engineering and product management counterparts on both sides to identify, scope, and deliver joint technical initiatives.</li> <li>Develop and lead joint go-to-market strategy for each partnership, connecting GitLab's business priorities, product roadmap, and AI strategy to concrete partner initiatives, and then own getting those plans executed.</li> <li>Build strong working relationships across partner organizations, including executives, product management, engineering, sales, and marketing stakeholders.</li> <li>Run a disciplined operating cadence across complex initiatives, with clear priorities, owners, timelines, coordination points, and follow-through you drive yourself.</li> <li>Coordinate cross-functional work inside GitLab to support partnership goals, aligning teams across product, engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and the executive group.</li> <li>Translate partner opportunities and requests into actionable internal plans, including roadmap discussions, integration needs, commercial terms, and executive recommendations.</li> <li>Track and communicate measurable partnership outcomes such as spend efficiency, consumption trends, renewal terms secured, integration progress, and joint go-to-market execution.</li> <li>Represent the partnerships at the executive level by preparing clear recommendations, briefing executives, and helping drive alignment on investments, trade-offs, and next steps.</li> </ul> <h3>What you'll bring</h3> <ul> <li>Significant experience owning strategic partnerships, alliance relationships, or vendor/commercial relationships in enterprise software, cloud, and/or AI, with a track record of being in the details, not just setting direction. This experience should reflect owning one or a small number of relationships in depth, not administering a large multi-partner channel ecosystem.</li> <li>Direct experience managing enterprise cloud commercial agreements (e.g., EDP, MACC, or similar consumption/spend commitments) with at least one major hyperscaler, including experience owning a renewal cycle from expiration planning through negotiation and close.</li> <li>Experience driving product or technical integrations with a cloud partner, and shaping joint go-to-market strategy that connects a product roadmap to partner initiatives.</li> <li>Strong ownership mindset with the ability to operate as a single-threaded owner who is accountable for both strategy and execution, and comfortable doing the hands-on work personally rather than handing it off.</li> <li>Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to distill complex commercial and partnership topics into clear recommendations for executives and cross-functional stakeholders.</li> <li>Strong project and program management skills, including the ability to organize complex workstreams, prioritize effectively, and keep multiple initiatives moving through direct, hands-on management.</li> <li>Genuine technical fluency in software development, platform integrations, and cloud infrastructure, with comfort engaging engineering and product counterparts in substantive conversations, not just positioning technology commercially.</li> <li>Experience working with senior stakeholders on high-visibility initiatives, including preparing executive briefings, framing recommendations, and driving follow-through.</li> <li>Ability to influence without formal authority, build strong working relationships across internal and external teams, and navigate multiple priorities with sound judgment.</li> <li>Familiarity with the DevSecOps ecosystem and a results-oriented approach to measuring partnership impact through spend efficiency and business/product outcomes rather than partner-sourced revenue or quota attainment.</li> <li>Preferred: candidates based in US Eastern or Central time zones, given close cross-functional coordination needs.</li> </ul> <h3>About the team</h3> <p>The Strategic Partnerships team owns the strategy and relationship management for some of GitLab's most consequential external partners, including the hyperscalers powering GitLab's infrastructure and future AI capabilities. We work across product, engineering, sales, marketing, finance, and the executive group to turn these partnerships into differentiated value for GitLab, manage our infrastructure investment responsibly, and ensure these relationships support our long-term platform strategy.</p> <p> </p><div class="content-pay-transparency"><div class="pay-input"><div class="description"><p><em>The base salary range for this role’s listed level is currently for residents of the United States only. Your work directly supports national security missions, including customers operating within FedRAMP-authorized, air-gapped, and classified or semi-classified environments where traditional troubleshooting approaches are not always possible.</p> <p>In this role, you will engage deeply with GitLab through the command line; analyzing logs, system behavior, and application performance with strong Linux fundamentals and an understanding of how GitLab’s components interact end-to-end. You may partner with Product and Engineering to reproduce and document edge-case defects using sanitized or redacted data, or contribute directly to the product by opening merge requests that resolve customer-impacting issues. Beyond resolving individual cases, you’ll help strengthen GitLab by improving documentation, support workflows, and institutional knowledge, ensuring that lessons learned in highly regulated environments benefit the broader platform; all while working in a fully remote, highly collaborative environment built on trust, autonomy, and shared ownership.</p> <p>Some examples of our projects:</p> <ul> <li value="1"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/strace-parser"><u><span class="textUnderline">A tool to quickly analyze strace output</span></u></a></li> <li value="2"><a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/toolbox/gitlabsos"><u><span class="textUnderline">A solution to capture the state of a customer’s server for easier troubleshooting</span></u></a></li> <li value="3"><a class="textLink" href="https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/chatops/"><u><span class="textUnderline">A functionality to ChatOps to make it easier to identify user accounts on GitLab.com</span></u></a></li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll do</strong></strong></h2> <ul> <li value="1">Collaborate closely with public sector customers, including U.S. government agencies, the Department of War, and Intelligence Community organizations, to diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve complex issues in GitLab deployments operating under strict security, compliance, and operational constraints.</li> <li value="2">Perform deep, hands-on technical investigations using Linux command-line tooling and GitLab internals to analyze logs, system performance, and application behavior, often with limited telemetry or incomplete datasets. You will trace issues across infrastructure, application, and code paths to identify root causes, recommend mitigations, and drive durable fixes; frequently partnering with GitLab Product, Development, and Infrastructure teams to ensure outcomes that meet both mission and platform reliability requirements.</li> <li value="3">Create and update clear, reusable documentation and support content based on real customer interactions to improve self-service and reduce repeated issues.</li> <li value="4">Participate in regular<a class="textLink" href="https://gitlab.com/gitlab-com/support/support-pairing/?_gl=1%2a1vj7usl%2a_ga%2aMTYyOTI0OTAxNC4xNjc4NzIwMDg0%2a_ga_ENFH3X7M5Y%2aMTY4NDgzNDU0OC4xMTAuMS4xNjg0ODM2NDM3LjAuMC4w"> <u><span class="textUnderline">pairing sessions</span></u></a> with other Support Engineers and act as a<a class="textLink" href="https://about.gitlab.com/handbook/support/#support-stable-counterpart"> <u><span class="textUnderline">stable counterpart</span></u></a> to cross-functional teams to share knowledge and improve support processes.</li> <li value="5">Contribute to building and refining internal support tools and workflows, including automation and troubleshooting utilities, to make diagnosing and resolving issues more efficient.</li> <li value="6">Participate in weekday and weekend on-call rotations, providing timely emergency support for self-managed customers operating in restricted and compliance-focused environments.</li> <li value="7">Support the growth of the team by reviewing applications and assessments, and participating in interviews and hiring decision discussions.</li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">What you’ll bring</strong></strong></h2> <ul> <li value="1">Due to government security requirements, you must be a United States Citizen (defined as any individual who is a citizen of the United States by law, birth, or naturalization) to be eligible for this position</li> <li value="2">Experience managing customer-facing cases across the full support lifecycle, from initial inquiry and triage through reproduction, escalation, and resolution</li> <li value="3">Strong Linux systems administration knowledge, with the ability to troubleshoot performance and configuration issues in complex environments</li> <li value="4">Familiarity with AI/LLM-powered developer tooling and gateway architectures (for example GitLab Duo, AI gateway configurations, or similar model-serving/proxy layers), including how they're deployed and troubleshot in self-managed or air-gapped environments</li> <li value="5">Ability to use scripting languages (preferably Ruby or Bash) and work within model-view-controller frameworks (preferably Ruby on Rails) to investigate and resolve issues</li> <li value="6">Practical experience with Git and continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) workflows</li> <li value="7">Skill in creating and maintaining clear, accurate support content and technical documentation</li> <li value="8">Ability to explain complex technical topics in a clear, empathetic way to customers and coworkers with varying technical backgrounds</li> <li value="9">Familiarity with DevOps practices and container-orchestration technologies such as OpenShift and Kubernetes</li> <li value="10">Understanding of common information security and compliance concepts and controls (for example DISA STIG and SELinux), and eligibility to work on United States federal customer environments as required for this role</li> </ul> <h2><strong><strong class="textBold">About the team</strong></strong></h2> <p>At GitLab Federal, LLC, the U.S. Government Support Engineering team partners with public sector organizations and United States government agencies to support GitLab in highly secure, mission-critical environments. Our work directly enables national security outcomes, supporting customers across the Intelligence Community, Department of War, and other federal, state, and local government entities operating within regulated and restricted boundaries.</p> <p>We are embedded within Support Engineering and work closely with Product, Development, Infrastructure, Customer Success, and Sales to solve complex, high-impact technical challenges. You’ll use editorial judgment, data, and cross-functional collaboration to create clear, inclusive, and authentic candidate experiences.</p> <p><strong>What You’ll Do</strong>  </p> <ul> <li campaigns across careers content, social media, employer review platforms, talent communities, events, and recruiter channels.</li> <li value="3">Develop and curate stories featuring team members, value="6">Use content, channel, candidate feedback, and funnel metrics to improve performance and communicate impact.</li> <li value="7">Collaborate across GitLab to ensure content is accurate, inclusive, culturally relevant, and aligned with our voice.</li> <li value="8">Manage projects and external partners while improving talent brand processes, systems, reporting, and operations through iteration and thoughtful use of technology and artificial intelligence tools.</li> </ul> <p><strong>What You’ll Bring </strong></p> <ul> <li value="1">Experience in talent brand, employer brand, recruitment marketing, content strategy, communications, or a related field.</li> <li value="2">Experience translating a brand or employer value proposition into content, campaigns, or audience experiences.</li> <li value="3">Strong storytelling, writing, editing, and editorial judgment across multiple channels.</li> <li value="4">Experience planning and delivering campaigns or programs with multiple stakeholders, dependencies, and deadlines.</li> <li value="5">Comfort using performance data, audience insights, feedback, and market research to improve outcomes.</li> <li value="6">Experience influencing across functions and working with senior stakeholders, subject matter experts, creative partners, or vendors.</li> <li value="7">Ability to manage ambiguity, prioritize competing work, and move from strategy to detailed execution in an asynchronous environment.</li> <li value="8">A commitment to inclusive, transparent storytelling, alignment with GitLab’s values and remote working practices, and applicable work authorization.</li> </ul> <p><strong>About the team</strong></p> <p>The GitLab Talent Brand team helps candidates understand what it means to work here through marketing, storytelling, partnerships, candidate education, and recruiter enablement. We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion. Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work. This internship will take place from May 24 - August 13 or June 14 - September 3 (based on your summer schedule) and you will need to be able to work out of our NY office during this time. ABOUT THE ROLE The Web Infrastructure team’s mission is to own the foundation of Notion’s web-based clients and to empower engineers to build performant, scalable, and accessible product experiences within them. title: People — Employment and Labor Law  (France)
description: Health can’t wait . Not for symptoms to get worse. Not for a six‑month appointment. Not for a system to catch up. But that’s exactly how healthcare works today. You wait, until you can’t. Alan exists to end the wait. Health is a universal right, and we believe this right can only become real when it’s coupled with prevention. We need to stop treating health as something we repair and start treating it as something we build, every day. It’s not solely a question of willpower. It’s the healthcare system itself that needs to work for everyone, in a sustainable way. So we are building the new standard in prevention insurance. Alan is the first company that integrates insurance, prevention, and care into a single, acclaimed user experience. We are on an incredible journey to build a global leading company, with a unique culture . We already partner with 40K+ companies of all sizes, serving more than 1M+ members, and have reached €800M+ in ARR. Prevention as the new norm. That's what we're building with our team of 1000+ people. If it speaks to you: we're hiring across France, Spain, Belgium, and Canada. And beyond. The Employment & Labour Law role 🇫🇷 Alan is growing fast: new health services, new entities, new countries, and a 2027 People agenda with social elections and many individual situations. Each of these brings legal obligations, and today we rely mostly on external counsel. In Alan's terms, "compliance" means everything we do to follow a mandatory rule that would become a risk if we got it wrong. The role makes sure Alan's employment practices are legally secure, pragmatic and humane. You will be our in-house expert on French employment and labour law, for both individual and collective matters. You are a People teammate first, with a strong legal foundation. Scope Alan operates in 8 countries. This role is based in France and covers French employment and labour law. It works in tandem with the People Compliance owner, who covers the other countries, and with the International Expansion hire for new country openings. Curiosity for other jurisdictions is a plus, but it is not the core of the role. You will join the People team, work closely with the People Compliance owner, the People lead and the individual situations crew, and be mentored by Alan's Compliance Key Function on how we practise legal topics at Alan. The People team The People team is made up of 13 people who work in an environment shaped by Alan's Leadership Principles. Every one of them is a genuine fan of our products (Culture being one of them) and deeply committed to Alan's Prevention and Health mission. The team covers Learning and Development, Payroll and Admin, Employee Experience and Operational Efficiency, Compliance and Employment Law, Comp and Ben, and M&A and International Expansion. It is a generalist team: everyone shares core missions, including individual situation management and HRBP responsibilities. Then each person owns one or more cross-functional topics depending on their flavour. In your case: French employment and labour law. Your missions On top of the core missions shared across the People team, you will work on a diverse range of high-impact topics: Employment law expertise: be the go-to person on French individual and collective employment law, with a strong focus on working time, night work and on-call rules (astreinte, rest periods), where the rules are strict and a creative, well-grounded approach makes a difference. Legal watch: monitor French labour-law changes, flag what matters for Alan, and use AI agents for legal watch and ongoing compliance checks. Obligations register: turn obligations into simple tools and processes, tracked in a register. Health and safety at work. Audits and inspections: support labour inspections, URSSAF audits and the related compliance reporting. Social dialogue: support the People lead in preparing CSE information-consultations, running the 2027 social elections, and drafting and updating company agreements (working time, profit-sharing, agreements for new services). Corporate structure: work through the People impact of Alan's evolving legal entities, such as which entities sit in the UES and what it means for our agreements. New services: bring a risk-based view early to projects with People impact, such as new health services, and help set up processes that protect Alan while keeping the flexibility and autonomy we want Alaners to have. External counsel: write clear briefs, ask sharper questions, reuse existing frameworks and challenge the advice you receive. Beyond France (occasionally): contribute, when needed, to topics in other countries, alongside the People Compliance owner. Raising the team's expertise: share your legal knowledge with the crew and the wider People team. AI and automation: use them to multiply the impact of your work. Outcomes within your first months in the team By 2.5 months You have contributed to a live CSE topic (e.g. preparing an information-consultation) and to at least one other live topic (e.g. working-time or on-call policy, an agreement for a new service). You have shadowed and been reverse-shadowed on individual situation management. By 5 months You own CSE information-consultations end to end, and a workstream such as a company agreement, with the crew as a sounding board. You are involved in preparing the 2027 social elections. You handle French individual situations without supervision, including the legal analysis. A first legal-watch automation is running. Crew members and leads come to you as the go-to expert on French employment law. Is this what you are looking for? You may be a great fit for this role if: You have a legal background in French employment and social law (e.g. M2 in droit social). You have around 4+ years of hands-on experience applying French employment law, typically in a law firm (ideally international), or you are a lawyer who has already moved into a People role. You master both individual and collective matters. You are excellent in French (negotiation level) and professional in English (our internal processes and documentation are in English). You put context before opinion: you understand how Alan works first, then adapt the playbook instead of applying it as is. You put business value before legal reflex: you start from the outcome and creative options, tell material risk from theoretical risk, and give practical answers. You are comfortable with a scale-up's risk appetite. You have a transversal mindset: a strong anchor in labour law, and real appetite to cover compliance, expansion and other topics. You are autonomous: you take initiative, flag risks early and own your outputs. You are rigorous: your work is precise and your writing is clear and concise. You are curious and coachable: open to feedback, with a clear idea of what you want to learn. You are AI-enthusiastic: you already use AI in your daily work and stay critical of the output. title: Technical Account Manager (APJ)
description: ABOUT SUPABASE Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth. ABOUT THE ROLE We’re seeking a Technical Account Manager (TAM) to be the primary technical partner for our Team & customers after the sale, helping them adopt, operate, and get long-term value from Supabase. At Supabase, TAMs are the technical owners of their assigned accounts, working closely with our most valuable customers to: - Understand each customer’s architecture, use cases, constraints, and goals. - Validate deployments and guide customers through onboarding and early success. - Proactively surface risks and optimization opportunities before they become incidents. - Coordinate internal teams on complex escalations and drive root cause analysis. - Align Supabase capabilities with the customer’s roadmap. Successful TAMs are proactive, technically credible, and customer-first. TAM is a relationship, not a response channel: you’ll act as an extension of your customers’ teams and advocate on their behalf within Supabase. You’ll be joining our Success team, where you will be expected to lead and innovate around the following areas of responsibility: Technical Ownership & Onboarding Act as the technical owner for your assigned accounts, documenting environments, mapping dependencies, and tracking technical risks. Validate architecture and deployment plans after the sale, guide initial configuration and best practices, and make sure customers understand platform capabilities and limitations. Help customers reach early success milestones to shorten time to value and reduce early friction. Proactive Technical Guidance Regularly review customer environments and usage patterns to identify scalability, performance, reliability, security, and compliance risks and opportunities. Plan upgrades and lifecycle events, and run architecture reviews for upcoming initiatives, including capacity and growth planning, feature readiness, and early identification of technical blockers. Escalation & Collaboration Coordinate across Support and Engineering on complex or high-impact issues. TAMs are not frontline support, but provide the context, prioritization, and follow-through that drive resolution, root cause analysis, and preventative action. Serve as the voice of the customer to Engineering and Product, sharing specific, reproducible feedback on recurring pain points and taking part in beta and early access programs. Partner with Sales and Customer Success on account health and retention, with technical input on renewals, expansions, and evaluations, and early flags on risks to satisfaction. PREFERRED EXPERIENCE 6+ years of relevant work experience in engineering, SRE, technical consulting, or similar, including operating production systems under real constraints. Strong technical depth across database internals, scalability, security posture, and infrastructure tradeoffs. You understand a customer’s architecture as well as they do, without escalating every question. A proactive mindset: you spot risks and optimization opportunities before the customer does, and you treat your accounts like a personal portfolio. Sound escalation judgment: you know when to escalate, when to resolve internally, and how to communicate clearly under pressure without creating noise. Very strong communication skills. TAMs explain complex issues to non-technical executives and root causes to senior engineers, often in the same day. Awareness of how TAM performance shows up in retention and NRR, including surfacing expansion signals and renewal risks early. Experience working in async or globally distributed teams. WHAT WE OFFER - Fully Remote We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world. - ESOP Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together. - Tech Allowance Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work. - Health Benefits Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us. - Annual Off-Sites Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year. - Flexible Work We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. title: Senior CRO & Funnel Marketing Manager (m/w/d) · Remote
description: Du hast schon Onlineshops zum Wachsen gebracht und suchst ein Umfeld, in dem du auf höchstem Niveau arbeiten kannst? Dann übernimm bei EVOLVE die Conversionrate-Optimierung und Funnelentwicklung von E-Commerce-Brands, von der ersten Analyse bis zum messbaren Ergebnis. Über EVOLVE Wir sind ein ganzheitlicher Wachstumspartner für E-Commerce-Brands im DACH-Raum. Jedes Jahr verwalten wir über 60 Millionen € Adspend und denken jedes Projekt von der Ad über den Funnel bis zur Marge. Unser Name ist Programm: Wir entwickeln uns, unsere Dienstleistung und unsere Kunden ständig weiter. Das spiegelt sich auch in unserer Mitarbeiterbewertung auf kununu mit 4,8 von 5 Sternen wider. Haben wir dein Interesse geweckt? Dann schau dir an, was dich bei uns erwartet. Das wirst du tun Du bist verantwortlich für verkaufsstarke Shopseiten und Funnels, die dafür sorgen, dass unsere Kunden den Markt outperformen. Analyse: Du analysierst Shops, Landingpages und Funnels ganzheitlich und leitest daraus priorisierte Hypothesen und Maßnahmen ab Positionierung: Du deckst die entscheidenden Hebel in der Customer Journey auf und entwickelst Positionierungen, die Marken klar vom Wettbewerb abheben Konzeption: Du erstellst conversionstarke Shop- und Landingpage-Konzepte und steuerst die Umsetzung mit UX-Design und Copywriting Kunden und Projekte: Du führst Kunden eigenständig durch den Optimierungsprozess und verantwortest Projekte bis zum messbaren Ergebnis Trends: Du verfolgst die aktuellsten Trends im Brand- und Direct-Response-Marketing und bringst sie in unsere Methodik und Standards ein Deine Rolle und deine Ressourcen: Du übernimmst von Anfang an Verantwortung für deine eigenen Projekte, stehst damit aber nicht allein: Unsere Experten für UX-Design, Copywriting und Performance Marketing setzen deine Konzepte mit dir um. Dich erwartet ein Team, das für Ergebnisse, Verlässlichkeit und kreative Exzellenz steht, mit flachen Hierarchien und einer offenen Feedbackkultur. Das bringst du mit Mindestens zwei Jahre Erfahrung in CRO, E-Commerce oder UX, idealerweise in einer Agentur oder einem Shop mit relevantem Traffic Sicherer Umgang mit GA4, Hotjar/Clarity und A/B-Tests Fundiertes Verständnis für Positionierung, Customer Journey und Conversion-Psychologie Klare Kommunikation, schriftlich wie im Kundengespräch Hohe Eigenständigkeit: Du priorisierst konsequent und gibst klare Empfehlungen Der Rahmen 100 % Remote , kein Hybrid-Kompromiss Vollzeit mit einer 38-Stunden-Woche 30 Tage Urlaub Zweimal jährlich Team-Events und Workations Wöchentliche Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats, damit Remote nicht heißt, den ganzen Tag allein zu arbeiten Betriebliche Altersvorsorge, JobRad und Firmenfitness über Wellpass Steuerfreier Sachbezug von 50 € monatlich als Gutschein deiner Wahl Laptop deiner Wahl und hochwertige Homeoffice-Ausstattung Weiterbildungsbudget sowie interne und externe Quellen und Mentoren an deiner Seite Voller Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack Vielleicht fragst du dich gerade … „Wie viele Projekte betreue ich parallel?“ Wenige, dafür aber in der Tiefe. So kannst du dich wirklich in jede Marke reindenken. Du arbeitest nicht am Fließband, sondern begleitest deine Kunden langfristig und siehst, was aus deinen Konzepten wird. „Welche Rolle spielt AI bei euch?“ Eine große. ChatGPT und Claude werden deine besten Freunde, denn mit den modernsten AI-Workflows optimierst du deine Arbeit und das Ergebnis für deine Kunden. Dafür hast du vollen Zugriff auf unseren internen AI-Stack. So bleibt mehr Zeit für das, was wirklich zählt: die richtigen Ideen für deine Kunden. „100 % Remote, verliere ich da den Austausch?“ Nein. Wir sind eine Remote-Agentur, aber Persönlichkeit und Teamspirit bleiben erhalten. Du hast das Gefühl eines Office-Teams, nur ohne Lärm und ohne Fahrt ins Büro. Dafür sorgen regelmäßige Projektabstimmungen, unsere wöchentlichen Team-Recaps und Coffee Chats. Deine Ansprechpartnerin Vanessa, unsere HR-Managerin, ist dein erster Kontakt und freut sich auf deine Bewerbung. Find more English Speaking Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Customer Care Analyst & Ops - CDI
description: Green-Got est une institution financière française qui permet à chacun de choisir ce que son argent finance. Nous construisons l'infrastructure financière du monde de demain. Depuis janvier 2026, Green-Got est un Établissement de Paiement agréé par l'ACPR, supervisé par la Banque de France. Une reconnaissance qui nous place au niveau des acteurs réglementés de premier plan, et qui change en profondeur ce que nous construisons, et comment. Green-Got propose : Un compte de paiement associé à une carte pour payer et être payé au quotidien. Une gamme de placements financiers performants pour investir dans les entreprises de la transition. L'expérience membre est au cœur de ce modèle. C'est le socle sur lequel repose la confiance que nos membres nous accordent, et que l'équipe Customer Care entretient chaque jour. Green-Got en chiffres : 100 M€ de transactions traitées chaque mois ; 2,3 Md€ de transactions sécurisées depuis notre lancement ; 2 M€ de dons reversés à des projets de transition ; 4,8/5 sur Trustpilot ; 5 % de notre chiffre d'affaires pour soutenir directement des projets de terrain, en finançant directement la Fondation Green-Got. Le contexte : 📍 Locaux à Paris + télétravail, ouvert au full remote depuis ton pays de résidence ; 📄 CDI : contrat de 39h /semaine ; 💶 28–32K € selon profil ; 🗓 Prise de poste : au plus tôt. Chez Green-Got, le Customer Care est la voix de nos membres en interne, et la voix de Green-Got auprès d'eux, un rôle stratégique dans une institution financière qui grandit vite et qui doit tenir ses promesses 7 jours sur 7. Nos membres ont changé de dimension avec nous : Compte Premium, PER, compte commun, offre indépendant. Chaque nouveau produit génère de nouvelles questions, de nouvelles situations, de nouveaux défis. L'ouverture prochaine des services BtoB va encore élargir le périmètre. Nous cherchons quelqu'un qui aime comprendre, qui sait garder son calme sous pression, et qui considère chaque échange comme une opportunité d'améliorer le produit, pas juste de fermer un ticket. Tu es à l'aise avec les gens et rigoureux sur le fond. Les deux à la fois. Vos missions Tes missions : Membre de l'équipe Customer Care, tu es le point de relais central entre nos membres et toutes les équipes de Green-Got : produit, tech, compliance, marketing, impact. Ton périmètre est vivant : il évolue avec nos lancements, nos besoins, et la trajectoire de Green-Got. Ta capacité à t'adapter, à prioriser et à garder un haut niveau de qualité dans tous les contextes est ce qui nous permettra de grandir sereinement. FRONT - Relation membre 50 % Premier point de contact : tu réponds à nos membres sur tous nos canaux, chat (90 %), email (8 %), téléphone (2 %), avec clarté, empathie et dans les délais. Expertise produit : tu connais Green-Got sur le bout des doigts. Tu accompagnes nos membres sur leurs comptes, leurs transactions, leurs questions, et tu trouves la bonne réponse après investigation. Gestion des nouvelles situations : tu identifies, qualifies et résous les cas inédits. Tu es garant de la qualité du premier contact. RUN - Support opérationnel 35 % Voix des membres en interne : tu collectes, structures et remontes les besoins, frustrations et suggestions aux équipes produit, tech, marketing. Amélioration continue : tu optimises les process existants, challenges les workflows, et maintiens notre documentation (FAQ, process) à jour à chaque évolution produit. Suivi des incidents : tu identifies les bugs, les remontes aux équipes concernées et en assures le suivi jusqu'à résolution. Recette fonctionnelle : tu participes aux phases de test des nouvelles fonctionnalités avant mise en production. BUILD - Gestion de projet 15 % Initiative et ownership : tu identifies des leviers d'amélioration de l'expérience membre, tu définis des indicateurs, proposes et mets en œuvre des actions concrètes. Pilotage : tu mets en place les outils et routines nécessaires au suivi de tes projets et en garantis le résultat. Vos compétences L'empathie, la rigueur dans l'exécution et la capacité à rester serein quand ça s'accélère sont pour toi des réflexes naturels. Tu comprends que la qualité du service est un engagement, pas une intention. Nous cherchons quelqu'un qui en est convaincu. Chez Green-Got, nous sommes curieux, exigeants, collectifs, et nous allons vite. Sens du service : tu sais que derrière chaque ticket, il y a une personne. Tu ne fermes pas un ticket, tu résous un problème. Rigueur et organisation : tu priorises, tu documentes, tu assures un suivi sans failles. Aisance rédactionnelle : ton orthographe est irréprochable, tu adaptes le ton à chaque interlocuteur. La précision est ta signature. Curiosité analytique : tu aimes comprendre pourquoi une situation se produit, pas juste la résoudre. Tu identifies les patterns et tu les remontes. Gestion du stress : tu gardes ton calme quand la situation l'exige. La pression ne dégrade pas ta qualité. Anglais opérationnel : tu lis, tu réponds, tu échanges sans chercher tes mots. Nous avons des membres non francophones et nous en aurons davantage. Sensibilité à l'impact : la transition environnementale a une réelle importance pour toi. Tu comprends les enjeux et tu portes la mission de Green-Got avec sincérité. Appétence pour les outils numériques : Intercom, Notion, Slack, Aircall, et une vraie curiosité pour l'IA et l'automatisation appliquées au service client. Formation : BTS, IUT, école de commerce, IAE ou toute formation en lien avec la relation client. Une première expérience en care ou service client est un vrai plus. Avantages Green-Got entre dans une nouvelle phase. Avec l'agrément ACPR, nous construisons une expérience membre de premier plan , avec les personnes qui nous rejoignent maintenant. Le service client de demain ne se construit uniquement avec des scripts et des macros. Il se construit avec des personnes qui comprennent le produit, les membres, et l'enjeu de chaque interaction. Un rôle avec de l'impact réel : dans un secteur en pleine transformation, au contact direct de nos membres chaque jour. De vraies responsabilités : tu n'exécutes pas, tu contribues. Tes remontées terrain façonnent le produit. Apprentissage : aux côtés d'une équipe qui transmet, dans un environnement réglementaire de premier plan. Évolution : les profils les plus engagés grandissent avec nous et prennent des responsabilités clés. Flexibilité : remote possible depuis chez toi et partout en Europe. Équipe : ambitieuse, exigeante, déterminée, et qui passe de bons moments ensemble. Le package : CDI remote ou Paris. Rémunération : 28 - 32k, selon profil. BSPCE. Mutuelle santé Alan. Une journée d’équipe tous les semestres. Déroulement des entretiens : Envoie-nous ton CV et tout autre élément qui nous aide à jauger tes compétences et ta motivation. Call rapide pour faire connaissance. Si ça matche, on t’envoie un Business Case à préparer. Entretien en visio avec Vincent (Customer Care Manager) pour analyser le Business Case et te tester / te connaitre. Échange avec un ou plusieurs membres de l’équipe pour le fit culturel. Entretien avec Adèle (Head of Operations). Entretien avec Andréa (CEO). Nous avons hâte de te rencontrer ! Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

title: Product Engineering Lead
description: Location: Remote (EMEA) · Germany/Munich preferred - CET/CEST time zone Hi — I'm Grigory, co-founder and CTO at Secfix. At Secfix we're building security compliance systems for teams and agents to become and stay compliant with less effort. We're already the category leader in Europe. AI is changing how software gets built, and we're shaping the tools this new era requires. I've spent most of my career believing that the best engineering leaders aren't the ones who run the most meetings. They're the ones who make everyone around them faster, clearer, and more proud of their work — and they can do that because they've been through the hard technical problems themselves. Since we started, I've done the engineering management myself: 1:1s, hiring, design reviews, performance conversations. The team is 8 engineers and 2 product designers, and I'm spread across too many things. If we were a football team, we'd be a good regional side that just made it to the Bundesliga — talented, hard-working, winning quite a few games. Now we need a coach who's played at Champions League level and can take us there to win every week. That means a top-notch engineer who leads from the codebase. Someone who owns the technical decisions, sets the pace, and has product taste — who notices when a feature takes three weeks that should take one, and when it ships on time but isn't good enough. You'll ship every week and lead the team's biggest technical work — and as the team grows, you'll grow into managing it. You'll work directly with me. Two things matter most here: speed and taste. Most teams pick one. We need both to win. — Grigory Why Secfix exists Over 1.78 million SMBs in Europe need to comply with security frameworks — ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, SOC 2 — just to sell to enterprise customers. The process is manual, painful, and takes over a year. We automated it. Our platform integrates with a company's full tech stack — AWS, Azure AD, Jira, GitLab, GCP, and more — automatically extracts compliance evidence, and guides teams to certification in weeks instead of months. Our fastest customer was certified in 4 weeks instead of the industry-standard 12+ months. We've raised €17M in total (€12M Series A), backed by Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. We're on a profitable trajectory, growing fast, and building the team that will take us to own European market from SMBs to mid market. This space is not threatened by AI; it's amplified by it. Compliance requires deep domain expertise combined with automation. Our new AI product (CISO AI) is just getting started, and there's a huge amount of engineering work ahead: agentic workflows, intelligent evidence collection, context-aware policy generation, and more. What you'll actually do in the first 3 months This isn't a role where you show up and start running standups. There are no standups. Here's how the first quarter goes: Month 1: Ship. Get into the codebase and ship a meaningful feature with AI alongside the team. By the end of the month, the team should be bringing you their hardest technical questions — because you've earned it, not because of the title. Month 2: Make the team faster. Find where features take three weeks that should take one, and fix it — in tooling, in how we review and test, or in who's working on what. Start pairing and doing technical 1:1s with two or three engineers, focused on weekly output, quality, and how well they use AI. Month 3: Own technical hiring. Take over the technical interviews and build a process that runs without my oversight. Design the technical challenges, run the screens, make the calls. The next people we bring in should raise the pace again. I will be there but switch my focus to final interviews. What will the role look like beyond the first 3 months? After the first quarter, the job is the technical decisions — and, as the team grows, management. You own how the team builds: how engineers test, how they review each other's code and security, how the team is organised, and who we hire next. We're 8 engineers and 2 product designers today and plan to be around 16 within 12 months — you'll run the technical side of it. Most of your time stays in the code: you ship every week and own the specs, architecture, and reviews on our biggest projects. As the team grows, you'll take on 1:1s, growth conversations, and eventually managing the team. Here's what you'll be close to in the next months: Speed. You’ll refine our software development processes to keep the team operating at high velocity. Cycle time from spec to production is your number and accountability. Tooling, review flow, how work is split, who's on what — whatever moves it. Quality. Improve how engineers test and automate, how they review each other's code and security changes, and how the zero-bug policy survives a team of 20. Team and hiring. Technical interviews and mentoring now; 1:1s, growth conversations, and the EM role as we grow. AI in the craft — and in the management. Engineers already work with an established set of encoded skills and rules — there's a whole playbook; you keep pushing that. Same for your own work: hiring, 1:1s, the recurring stuff. What success looks like At 6 months: You've led at least 2-3 major projects from spec to production. The hiring process runs without me, and we've added 2 engineers through it. Sales, CS, and product all feel the difference in how fast we ship — and in quality. At 12 months: The team is around 12-16, the zero-bug policy is still holding at that size, and I'm not in the engineering critical path anymore. You've taken over 1:1s as the team grew, and you're ready to step into the EM role. How we work We've written in depth about our engineering culture. Here's the short version — read the full articles linked below if you want the real picture. Focus is sacred. Engineers are in fewer than 2 hours of meetings per week. We write before we meet. We use Loom for async walkthroughs, Notion for specs, Gather for pairing, and Slack only for what's urgent or lightweight. We don't do status theatre. We wrote about our thoughtful communication and our remote culture ; give it a read. To drive it home, here's a recent calendar of an engineer who has been with us for over a year: Small, temporary teams. A designer and two engineers. A backend engineer and a CS person. The group forms around the problem, ships, and dissolves. No standing squads, no permanent team structures — at least not yet. The people closest to the problem usually shape the solution. AI is already part of the craft. We use Claude for product design exploration and spec drafting. Engineers work in Cursor with encoded skills and rules that live in the codebase — component patterns, folder structure, architecture choices, and the path from Figma to Angular code. AI checks code against architecture rules before human review. We have a dedicated design QA skill that compares Figma against coded output. We don't use AI to lower the bar; we use it to reach the bar faster with more iterations behind us. In case you’re interested, we wrote a piece about it here . Zero-bugs. We take this seriously - this helps us to gain customer trust faster. Especially serious customer-facing problems don't sit in a backlog competing with roadmap work. Critical issues get fixed immediately. High-severity within 48 hours. Every bug has an owner. Weekly quality review as part of Monday planning. Quality as identity, in compliance, being correct isn't a nice-to-have; it's the entire value proposition. We care about edge cases, data integrity, and getting the details right. Customers notice the speed and polish before they can name it. That kind of quality builds trust. In our category, trust is the product. We build what customers need , not what they ask for. Customer feedback is signal, not instructions. Best products are built by people with great taste who treat feedback as signals, not KPIs. We stay close to customers — CS check-ins, support tickets, Mixpanel events, onboarding calls — but none of these sources makes the decision for us. This role is for you if: You've led a team technically and made it ship faster. You've set its technical direction, run its design reviews, and interviewed for it — and you can point to where cycle time dropped because of you. You know what great engineers look like. You've thought deeply about what makes them productive, what holds them back, and how to move them forward — and you can spot one in a single interview. You have an exceptional IC track record. You're a senior or staff engineer whose code and designs others build on — and you want to grow into managing, not escape coding. You have product taste. You notice when a feature ships on time but isn't good enough, and you say so. You hold people to a high standard. You're comfortable giving direct feedback and having hard conversations in code reviews and design discussions. You're hands-on with AI-assisted development. You've used Cursor and Claude Code in real production work, not just toy projects. You have opinions about how AI changes the engineering workflow from ideation to release, and you want to push a team to keep getting faster. You've worked in startups. You know what it feels like when there's low process, and the answer is "figure it out and ship it." You think engineering culture can stay startup-like at scale. You're optimistic that a small, high-performing team can stay that way as it grows, with little process. You communicate proactively in writing. In a remote team, written communication is how decisions get made and context gets shared. But you're not scared of jumping into a pair programming session either. What we're looking for Required 8+ years as a software engineer at senior or staff level, including 1+ years as a tech lead (formal or de facto) for a team of 3+ You've shipped AI features to production — retrieval, RAG, agentic workflows — and you know the difference between a demo that works and one that holds up on real customer data Product taste: a keen sense for what makes a product feel great, and the habit of saying so when it doesn't You've built and shipped with Claude Code and Cursor in real production work, and you have opinions about where AI helps and where it quietly creates debt You lead system design, not just contribute to it: you write the spec, own the architecture, and drive it to production Strong OOP fundamentals; Java Spring Boot, Hibernate, or equivalent Relational database design and SQL optimisation Experience interviewing engineering candidates You've built something zero to one at a startup, or scaled a team through the messy middle. You know what it feels like when there's no playbook Able to work in European timezone (CET/CEST). EMEA-based, ideally Germany or UK Nice to have Some people management and technical interviewing experience Designed a technical interview process from scratch Previous experience at a fully remote company Interview process We want to see how you think, build, and lead — not test you on algorithms. Here's the process: 30 min — Intro call with our talent team 45 min — Interview with Grigory 60 min — Technical interview 1.5 hr — AI-assisted build session: system design for a real feature, then building part of it with AI 2 hr — Leadership session with the founders Then you’ll get the offer! If we don't make an offer, we'll tell you why. What Secfix gives you Remote: 100% remote with a real virtual office in Gather Salary: Competitive, benchmarked to European market rates (we'll share specifics once we talk) Equity: Generous package — we're all owners here Development budget: €1,000/year — yours to spend on whatever makes you better Workspace: Remote workspace support + co-working access Holidays: 26 days + local public holidays Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage Annual retreat: Last time we went to Alicante 🇪🇸 — before that, the Austrian Alps, Portugal, Italy,

title: GRC Specialist
description: Remote from the UK, Germany, Austria, Poland, Montenegro or Serbia. At Secfix, we’re at the forefront of automating security compliance in Europe. We help companies get and stay ISO 27001, GDPR, TISAX, and SOC 2 fast and easy and reduce hundreds of hours of manual work. Secfix is run by a 100% remote team with hubs in Munich, Berlin and London. We’re a high-performing team looking for passionate, execution-focused, owners to help us automate security and compliance for modern companies and become the European compliance automation leader. We’ve just raised our $12M Series A and are backed by top VCs, including Alstin Capital, Neosfer (Commerzbank), and Bayern Capital. About the Role We're hiring a GRC Specialist (Governance, Risk and Compliance) to strengthen our compliance function as Secfix scales into more frameworks, mid-market customers, and a growing compliance team. This role sits at the intersection of compliance delivery, content, and team support. You'll own the compliance knowledge that lives inside our platform, run internal audits, support our customer success team, and act as the compliance voice for customers, auditors, and product. You'll work closely with our co-founder & CISO and our CS Lead. This is a high-impact role with real influence on how Secfix delivers compliance: both as a service to customers and as content inside our app. What You'll Do: You will own one of the most important pillars of Secfix: the quality and breadth of our compliance offering . We don't (and can't afford to) micro-manage. We've built strong foundations and will give you full context on what works. You can test new approaches, but at the end of the day, you have full ownership of how you deliver results (with a strong support network from within and outside the company). You will: Build and maintain compliance frameworks in the Secfix platform (ISO 27001, TISAX, SOC 2, GDPR, NIS 2, DORA, ISO 27017/27018, ISO 42001, C5, and more as we expand) Own internal audits for our customers end to end, from kickoff through to the final report they take into their external audit Keep several audits moving at once and keep every one on schedule Implement ISO 27001 and adjacent frameworks end-to-end for customers Own the quality of compliance content in the platform (including creating policies, automated checks, evidence templates, Compliance enable playbooks for our CSMs, security awareness trainings and more) Close framework gaps and incorporate auditor feedback into both team practice and platform improvements Partner with product and engineering to translate compliance gaps into structured product work Collaborate closely with CS, Product, and Founders to align compliance, customer, and roadmap priorities Deepen relationships with our existing certification partners and train auditors on the Secfix platform so they can confidently use it during customer audits To be qualified for this role, you must have the following: English (fluent) is a must for this role 3+ years of hands‑on information security and GRC experience Led at least 1 successful ISO 27001 certification projects as an implementer and/or auditor at a startup or mid-market company You have run at least 2 internal audits before. Hands on experience with a GRC platform like Secfix, or similar GRC platforms Real depth in at least one framework beyond ISO 27001 (TISAX, SOC 2, GDPR, NIS2, or similar). Strong project management skills with the ability to break down ambiguous initiatives into concrete deliverables, prioritizes ruthlessly, and ships Excellent written communication, especially in producing clear, precise compliance content for diverse audiences (auditors, founders, engineers) Strong ownership mindset: operates as an individual contributor without waiting for direction Bachelor's degree in computer science, software engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent hands-on technical experience. Bonus points for: Experience mentoring or coaching colleagues in a compliance, audit, or GRC context Experience in a startup environment is a plus A PECB ISO 27001 Lead Auditor certification or a direct equivalent Interview Process: Screening call with Talent team Take-home Assessment 1.5hr Assessment review and interview with our CS Lead and CEO 45 min - Final Founder Interview with Co-Founders (CTO & CISO) What we offer Remote Work: 100% remote work with a virtual office in Gather. Competitive Salary: Industry-competitive local salaries. We pay local rates that are at or above the market. We share this philosophy with GitLab. Equity: Generous equity package – we’re all owners of Secfix and beneficiaries of our collective success. Mentorship: We are backed by top VCs and accelerators and have direct access to world-class mentors. Development Budget: €1,000 annual personal development budget. Home office Budget: Home office budget and access to co-working spaces. Holidays: 26 days holiday + local public holidays. Health Insurance: Comprehensive health coverage. Annual Retreat: Annual retreat to build connections and inspire ideas (this year we’re headed to Milan!). Company Events: Company-wide events to build relationships and have some fun!
